227.content: Narfell is a dry, flat, infertile region of scrublands home to the Nars, nomadic horse-riding barbarian tribesmen, and dotted with numerous long-abandoned ruins of the fallen fiend-worshipping Narfell Empire, including the remnants of the imperial capital of Dun-Tharos. Marauding tundra yeti are a constant threat to Narfell's inhabitants. Hark's Finger, the ruins of a fallen Netherese enclave, juts from the scrublands. The Nars gather in the seasonal tent city of Bildoobaris to trade.

228.content: Rashemen is a barren, wind-swept realm of berserker clans ruled by the magocratic gynarchy of witches known as the Wychlaran, who appoint the Iron Lords to rule over the berserker lodges in Immilmar, the capital, and Thasunta, City of Warriors. The catacombs under the ruined Fortress of the Half-Demon are still said to contain creatures summoned by the lost Narfell Empire. The powerful lich Red Wizards of Thay and their undead legions are a constant threat to Rashemen.

229.content: The nation of Thesk is a wealthy, trade-oriented oligarchy of tolerant, open-minded merchants and farmers along the Golden Way, the main trade route to Kara-Tur. The independent port-city of Telflamm is publicly governed by a merchant prince but secretly ruled by thieves' guild known as the Shadowmasters. The inland areas of Thesk are subject to seasonal tornadoes.

230.content: Lantan is an island-nation of rock gnomes and humans dwelling in lush jungle known for its advanced technology: self-filling oil lamps, mechanical intruder alarms, clockwork devices and smokepowder-powered firearms such as arquebuses. Lantan is home to the High Holy Crafthouse of Inspiration of the Church of Gond, a large, walled monastery run by the High Artificer, as well as the famed gnomic College of Bards and Order of Fabulists.

231.content:
The capital of the wealthy mercantile nation of Calimshan is the sprawling port-city of Calimport, ruled by Emperor Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal and wealthy nobles called pashas. Enslaved genasi, planetouched descendants of genies, are common. Black Raider bandits rob the caravans that travel the trade routes of the rocky Calim Desert. The trade-rich Shining Sea is infested with corsairs. The wasteland known as the Plane of Stone Spiders is ruled by a demon called the Spider That Waits.



The capital of the wealthy mercantile nation of Calimshan is the sprawling port-city of Calimport, ruled by Emperor Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal and wealthy nobles called pashas. Enslaved genasi, planetouched descendants of genies, are common. Black Raider bandits rob the caravans that travel the trade routes of the rocky Calim Desert. The trade-rich Shining Sea is infested with pirate galleys. The wasteland known as the Plane of Stone Spiders is ruled by a demon called the Spider That Waits.

232.content: Tethyr is a wealthy feudal monarchy of tradesmen and merchants along the Trade Way governed by Queen Anais Rhindaun and her Royal Council from the Palace of Faentarn in the capital of Darromar. Enchanted Wealdath Forest, home to fey creatures, monsters and dragons, is the territory of the Elmanesse copper elves and Suldusk wild elves as well as a base of operations of cells of the Eldreth Veluuthra, dedicated to the removal of all humans from Faerûn.

233.content: The Moonshae Isles are a rocky, subarctic archipelago of fens, moorlands, forests and highlands. The port-city of Caer Callidyrr on the Isle of Aaron, ruled by noble House Kendrick, is the capital city of the peaceful Ffolk, known for their steel and galleon-building, enemies of the Northlander, brutal raiders and slave-traders. The Isle of Snowdown is ruled by the vampire Lady Erliza Daressin, the Isle of Oman by a tribe of fomorians and the Isle of Moray by Malarite lycanthropes.

234.content: The Nelanther Isles are a chain of inhospitable islands in the Trackless Sea dominated by ruthless orc, lizardfolk, ogre and minotaur pirates. The Port of Skaug is a cove of privateers and corsairs home to dockyards and taverns frequented by the dregs of society. The Isles are surrounded by treacherous reefs and shoals and conceal many hidden sea-grottoes, inlets, bays and coves.

235.content: Nimbral is a mysterious island nation of moon elf and human illusionists governed by the Nimbral Lords, an eccentric family of archmages dwelling in a complex of towers linked by sky-bridges, protected by the Knights of the Flying Hunt, an order of aerial pegasus-mounted champions dedicated to eradicating piracy from the isles.

236.content: Prosperous Cormyr is a war-torn land ruled by Queen Raedra Obarskyr from the stately capital of Suzail on Lake Dragonmere and protected by the War Wizards, an order of battlemages, and the Purple Dragons, an elite military corps. All adventurers in Cormyr require a charter from the Crown, but Cormyr's wealthy noble houses offer grants of land to those who aid them in defending the realm from orc and goblin armies and incursions by the Shadovar.

237.content: The Dragon Coast is a lawless region of cutthroat pirates, criminals and secret societies such as the Night Masks, Fire Knives assassins and druidic Fellowship of the Purple Staff. Bustling Elversult is home to the cult of Amaunator and is lit by the god's second sun shining in the sky. The squalid slumtown of Westgate, domain of crime syndicates and vampiric crime-lords, thrives on black-market trade and corruption and is home to the cult of evil gods such as Umberlee, Talos and Loviatar.

238.content: Hlondeth, the City of Serpents, ruled by the House Extaminos, a noble family of yuan-ti halfblood serpentfolk, is a graceful complex of emerald-green marble burrow-villas, round, coiled towers and spires. The environs of Hlondeth are home to draconic ssvaklors and spectral panthers. The nobles of Hlondeth keep serpentine histachii servitors, ophidians and flying snakes as pets and kobolds as slaves. Hlondeth is a home to a major temple of the serpent-god Sseth.

239.content: Sembia is a federation of mercantile city-states governed by merchant lords of prosperous merchant-noble households such as the Uskevren and Foxmantle based in the prosperous coastal capital of Selgaunt, plagued by rampant corruption by secret cabals and villainous cults.

240.content: Chondalwood is a constantly expanding forest home to treants, roving tribes of wild elves, satyrs, wood giants and centaurs, savage druids, ghostwise halflings, shambling mounds and tendriculos, all striving to protect Chondalwood against human encroachment. The anti-human Eldreth Veluuthra have an active cell in the Chondalwood, supported by the forest creatures. The mythical hidden elven city of Rucien-Xan is said to be located deep in Chondalwood.

241.content: Bildoobaris, or Trade Fair, is the unofficial capital of Narfell, a temporary tent city in a vast open plain where over 30,000 Nars gather one tenday every summer.

242.content:
Vampires are powerful blood-drinking undead night predators whose only weaknesses are sunlight, fire, decapitation and blood-hunger, which drives them to bestial acts of degenerate fury. Vampires can regenerate wounds, shape-change into mist, charm the living into doing their bidding and fight with supernatural speed and strength. The curse of vampirism can be transmitted by a vampire's bite.



Vampires are powerful blood-drinking undead night predators whose only weaknesses are sunlight, fire, decapitation and blood-hunger.

243.content:
Avariel (aril-tel-quessir, or "winged folk" in Elven) are a race of good-aligned, winged sky-elves hailing from the Aerie of the Snow Eagles at the edge of the Great Glacier. Avariel worship Aerdrie Faenya and have a strong affinity for other good-aligned flying races such as the aarakocra.



Avariel are a race of good-aligned, winged sky-elves hailing from the Aerie of the Snow Eagles at the edge of the Great Glacier. Avariel worship Aerdrie Faenya and have a strong affinity for other good-aligned flying races such as the aarakocra.

244.content:
Tabaxi are clannish jaguar-folk with spotted or striped fur, long feline tails and retractable claws. Though reclusive by nature, tabaxi are driven by intense, feline curiosity to explore, thriving on the thrill of the hunt, be it for prey or artefacts to study, but quickly lose interest upon attaining their objective, moving on to the next quest.



Tabaxi are clannish jaguar-folk with spotted or striped fur, long feline tails and retractable claws.

245.content:
Aasimar are planetouched humanoids descended from good celestials. Aasimar are revered and feared for their celestial lineage, which grants remarkable insight, natural allure, an innate ability to cast supernatural light and an inclination for divine magic and service to the gods.



Aasimar are planetouched humanoids descended from good celestials. Aasimar are revered and feared for their celestial lineage, which grants remarkable insight, natural allure, an innate ability to cast supernatural light and an inclination towards divine magic and service to the gods.

246.content:
Arctic dwarves are a race of hardy hunter-gatherer snow-dwarves native to the Great Glacier. In their icy native clime, arctic dwarves live in snow-houses, leading a communal lifestyle and waging perpetual war against their sworn enemies, the frost giants.



Arctic dwarves are a race of hardy hunter-gatherer snow-dwarves native to the Great Glacier.

247.content:
Lizardfolk are powerfully built reptilian humanoids with scaly skin, muscular tails, sharp claws and fangs. Lizardfolk tend to be primitive, savage tribal creatures with voracious appetites who hail from swamps and wetlands and eschew urban settlements. Most lizardfolk worship Semuanya, amoral reptilian god of survival and procreation.



Lizardfolk are powerfully built reptilian humanoids with scaly skin, muscular tails, sharp claws and fangs.

248.content:
Robust, muscular humanoids with porcine features and boar-like tusks, orcs are an action-oriented, quick-tempered race of despotic, warlike tribes notorious for conquering and occupying the settlements of other races and taking their women as chattel slaves.



Orcs are robust, muscular humanoids with porcine features and boar-like tusks who live in warlike tribes notorious for conquering and enslaving other races.

249.content:
Werewolves are savage shape-changing predators with humanoid, full wolf and hybrid form, in which a furred, muscular body is topped by a wolf's head. Weak to silver and magic, they are cursed to turn in the full moon, and often live as outcasts, hunting in packs in the wild led by fierce alpha lycanthropes and dire wolves. The curse of lycanthropy can be spread by a werewolf's tooth or claw wound or inherited.



Werewolves are savage shape-changing predators who can take humanoid, full wolf and hybrid forms.

250.content:
Bigger and stronger than the goblins and smarter than the bugbears they command, hobgoblins rule over other goblinoids in mixed-race martial societies, breeding drakes and wargs to obey their orders in their wars of conquest.



Hobgoblins are bigger and stronger than the goblins and smarter than the bugbears they command, allowing them to rule over other goblinoids in mixed-race martial societies.

251.content:
Kobolds are diminutive mischievous reptilian humanoids with scaly skin, claws and tails. A reclusive, spiteful race, kobolds excel at mining and trap-making, dwelling in isolated tribal societies in dark forests or underground lairs. Kobolds are sensitive about their small size and fiercely resentful of larger races.



Kobolds are diminutive mischievous reptilian humanoids with scaly skin, claws and tails.

252.content:
Aarakocra bird-men are flying avian humanoids who live in tribes on mountain peaks.



Aarakocra are flying avian humanoids who live in tribes on mountain peaks.

253.content: The Guild is a thieves' guild in Baldur's Gate that oversees all aspects of organized crime in the city, from thugs, burglars and con men to protection rackets, gambling rings and smuggling. A Kingpin is in charge of each district. At the top of the Guild's hierarchy is secretive Guildmaster Nine-fingers Keene.

254.content: The Chasm is a massive sealed rift running through Neverwinter. Though it has now been sealed, signs of plagueland such as blue fires and warped reality can still be seen over the sealed Chasm, and many plaguechanged creatures still hide within the city.

255.content: The Yawning Portal is an inn in the Castle Ward of Waterdeep. The inn is known for containing the main entrance to the dungeon of Undermountain, accessible through a well, into which adventurers may be lowered for a fee of one gold piece. The Yawning Portal inn offers healing services provided by a cleric of Tymora. The inn is patronized by Waterdeep’s adventurers, who meet there to organize exploration of Undermountain. Patrons of the Yawning Portal also gamble on the success or failure of expeditions. The owner and bartender of the Yawning Portal is retired dungeon-delver Durnan, a gruff, burly human whose hatred of injustice has also led him to found the vigilante group the Red Sashes.

256.content: Plaguechanged creatures have been corrupted and mutated into aberrations by the wild magic of plaguelands. Plaguechanged creatures may be recognized by the blue flames they manifest.

257.content: Fomorians are a race of fallen former elves, warped into grotesque, wicked giants by an ancient curse, which they can pass on with the deforming power of the evil eye. Some fomorians form pacts with the Gloaming Court or eldritch entities to gain mastery over shadows. Others are witches obsessed with using their evil eye curse to alter their bodies to more desirable forms through alchemy or to create deformities in others. Native to the Feydark and Underdark, fomorians are vicious, paranoid, cruel and patriarchal, plotting to conquer and subjugate their hated elven and eladrin ancestors. Fomorians keep cyclopes, gnomes, xvarts, myconids, and spriggans as their slaves.

258.content: Fey eladrin are elves from the Feywild. Fey eladrin have supernatural abilities: changing their appearance and powers to match their mood, teleportation, channeling and taking on characteristics of the seasons.

259.content:
Acquisitions Incorporated is a company of groups of adventurers for hire known as franchises. Each adventuring franchise competes for territory and exclusivity rights, assigned by the head office. Founder Omin Dran is a half-elf Masked Lord of Waterdeep and cleric of Tymora. The company headquarters is in the basement of the Silver Unicorn Inn, in the city of Fallcrest. A franchise known as the C Team is based in the Dran & Courtier inn in Red Larch.
Company rivals include Dran Enterprises, led by an impersonator of Omin Dran's sister Auspicia, and the Six, a company of adventurers wronged as a result of Acquisitions Incorporated's operations. Other well-known members include Jim Darkmagic, Flabbergast and Phoenix Anvil.

260.content: The Dark Seldarine is the drow pantheon. The Dark Seldarine are made up of Lolth, Eilistraee (goddess of beauty, dance, song, freedom, moonlight, swordwork, hunting), Ghaunadaur (god of subterranean, jellies, oozes, outcasts, rebels, ropers, slimes), Kiaransalee (goddess of undead, necromancy, vengeance), Selvetarm (god of drow warriors, slaughter) and Vhaeraun (god of drow males, evil activity on the surface, territory, thievery, arrogance).

261.content:
Neverwinter is a cosmopolitan city-state famed for its mild climate and lush gardens. A massive rebuilding project is underway to repair the damage from the Mount Hotenow eruption. Lord Protector of Neverwinter, iron-fisted Dagult Neverember, is intent on rebuilding the city into a mercantile empire, forging ties with the dwarves of Gauntlgrym and putting down the rebellion by the Sons of Alagondar. The Neverwinter Guard patrols the city against orc infestation, Luskan raids and infiltration by Ashmadai cells. The fortified Protector's Enclave is the seat of government and Castle Never. Efforts to rebuild the Blacklake District and River District after the eruption have stalled due to opposition from the Ashmadai and Sons of Alagondar. Though the Chasm has been sealed, the occasional deformed plaguechanged can still be found in Neverwinter, and the Abolethic Sovereignty still lurks in the depths beneath the city.



Neverwinter is a cosmopolitan city-state famed for its mild climate and lush gardens kept in perpetual bloom by the balmy Neverwinter River. A massive rebuilding project is currently underway following the Mount Hotenow eruption in 1451 DR. Lord Protector of Neverwinter, iron-fisted Dagult Neverember, is intent on rebuilding the city into a mercantile empire, forging ties with the dwarves of Gauntlgrym and putting down the rebellion by the Sons of Alagondar.

262.content: House Phylund is a noble family of Waterdeep whose business is acquiring, taming, training and selling fierce beasts. The Phylunds have a compound in the North Ward of Waterdeep and the Phylund Hunting Lodge in Ardeep Forest, which they use as a base for monster hunting safari expeditions. The Phylunds hire adventures to help capture, breed, and sell monsters as pets, guard beasts, and arena fighters.

263.content: The Far Realm is a plane of madness that twists visitors into monsters and is the source of aberrations. Mind flayers, aboleths, beholders, carrion crawlers, kaorti and uvuudaum are native to the Far Realm.

264.content: Gauntlgrym is a rediscovered ancient dwarfhold under the Crags range and Mount Hotenow near Neverwinter. Once occupied by drow from Menzoberranzan, it has been reclaimed by dwarves led by King Bruenor Battlehammer.

265.content:
The Xanathar Thieves' Guild is a powerful network of criminals, mercenaries, slavers, pirates and assassins with a massive stronghold in the subterranean city of Skullport under Waterdeep. The Guild is run by the Xanathar, a paranoid elder beholder. To join, one must kill or sell a family member into slavery. Agents of the Xanathar Thieves' Guild are assigned companions (bugbear, wererat, kenku, gazer) who spy and report on their performance. Guild-members often kill each other to advance.



The Xanathar Thieves' Guild is a powerful network of criminals, mercenaries, slavers, pirates and assassins run by the Xanathar, a paranoid elder beholder with a stronghold in the subterranean city of Skullport beneath Waterdeep and a shadowy web of operations throughout the Sword Coast and much of Faerûn.

266.content:
Force Grey, or the Gray Hands, are an elite corps of veteran adventurers who protect Waterdeep from extreme supernatural and arcane threats and enemies too dangerous for the City Guard and City Watch. Reporting directly to the Lords of Waterdeep and the Blackstaff, Grey Hands put down emergencies and act as an elite strike force. Grey Hands are notorious for their gung-ho brute force, collateral damage and havoc.



Force Grey, or the Gray Hands, are an elite corps of veteran adventurers who protect Waterdeep from threats and enemies too dangerous for the City Guard and City Watch to handle.

267.content:
The Heralds of Faerûn are impartial, neutral scholars, diplomats, keepers of heraldic lore and experts in courtly etiquette, rules of inheritance, genealogy, coats of arms, and history. Heralds arbitrate disputes and serve as emissaries, members of diplomatic missions between kingdoms, liaisons between noble houses and information brokers between bards and sages. Heralds may act as stewards or war commanders in civil wars or regents in disputed successions. High Heralds are the most senior members, followed by the Heralds Pursuivant. Herald's Holdfast is a spellguarded library complex near Silverymoon, and Herald's Hall is a secret headquarters in an opulent manor on an island on a subterranean lake near Amn, home to the Herald known as Unicorn.



The Heralds of Faerûn are a group of historians, lore-keepers, diplomats and scholars. Famed for their impartiality and neutrality, Heralds are often called in to mediate in disputes or resolve disagreements between noble families or realms.

268.content: The Shadowfell, or Plane of Shadow, is a dark, warped echoworld, a dimension without color and light, only shades of darkness, home to the uncity of Evernight and Shadow Keep, domain of Shar, Mask and Null. In addition to humanoid denizens known as shades, the Shadowfell is inhabited by bodaks, cloakers, darkweavers, ephemera, veserabs, liches, nightshades, shadar-kai, spectres, and wraiths.

269.content: Sea Ward is Waterdeep's wealthiest district of imposing stone banks, stately guildhouses and opulent temples such as the House of the Moon, dedicated to Selûne, and the House of Heroes, dedicated to Tempus. Sea Ward is home to the Field of Triumph gladiators' arena, where adventurers go to test their mettle as gladiators or wager on the gladiatorial contests. Renowned magic school Eltorchul Academy is based in the House Eltorchul family villa in Sea Ward. The lush park of Heroes' Garden is said to conceal an entrance to Undermountain. Dragon Tower, a wizard’s tower shaped to resemble a rampant dragon, with smoke pouring from its nostril-chimneys, is said to be home to gold dragon Aurinax.

270.content: Following the defeat of the drow in the Cormanthor War, the elves are returning the ancient forest of Cormanthor to repopulate their ancestral woodland homes. The ancient capital of Myth Drannor has been resettled and restored under Ilsevele Miritar. Tangled Trees is a hidden realm of tree-forts, elevated platforms and skyways in Cormanthor where xenophobic elves worship Rillifane Rallathil and attack non-elves who dare to trespass.

271.content: Valamaradace, Dragon Queen of Silverymoon, is an ancient gold dragon who lairs in the Floating Mountain, an enormous hollow rock that hovered above the woods near Everlund.

272.content: House Extaminos is a yuan-ti tribe. The yuan-ti of Extaminos conduct scientific experiments using magic, drugs and training to create subservient guardians and servants. Extaminaar graft magical appendages onto their bodies. Extaminos is based in Hlondeth in the Vilhon Reach, but the Extaminaar have infiltrated many cities and control various thieves' guilds' and adventuring groups.

273.content: Zelifarn is a friendly, inquisitive bronze dragon who has taken up residence in a hidden sea cave in Waterdeep’s harbor. Zelifarn dives to explore shipwrecks at the bottom of the harbor for treasure. Zelifarn keeps all his findings in a secret underwater cave.

274.content: Hark's Finger is a mountain that juts from the flatlands of Narfell. The Nar call it Mount Jiksidur and consider it a sacred place and a gift from the gods. Few are those who know the truth: Hark’s Finger is an ancient Netherese enclave named Jiksidur that plummeted from the sky when Netheril fell.

275.content: The Black Jungles are a dense forest in Tashalar on the Chultan Peninsula. Hidden deep in the Black Jungles is the ruined Pit of Vipers, once a vast stronghold and temple of Sseth, the World Serpent. The Pit of Vipers complex is guarded by histachii protecting the brood chambers. Yuan-ti explore the ruins of the temple, once the capital of Serpentes during Sseth's ascendancy.

276.comment: the House of the All-Seeing Orb
276.content: The House of the All-Seeing Orb, temple to Savras, is a center of study of divination in Tashluta. It is a vast complex of fine courtyards and buildings, emblazoned with the all-seeing eye of Savras.

277.content: Savras is the god of divination, fate, and truth. Savras' symbol is a monstrous eye or a crystal ball filled with eyes.

278.content:
Valin Sarnaster is a notorious, powerful seer of Savras. Although she is a mummy lord, Valin appears young and beautiful, her appearance altered by her magical diadem. Valin lives in a crypt in the House of the All-Seeing Orb in Tashalar. Valin Sarnaster's mind is warped by visions of grandeur; she believes she is destined to ascend to divinity as the demigod of fate and usurp the god Savras. She has created an army of canopic golem servants to aid her in her schemes.
Valin can only be destroyed by destroying her crystalline heart, hidden in the chest of her most loyal devotee.

279.content: The Trades Ward is Waterdeep's main commercial district. The Bowels of the Earth tavern is the place to find adventurers. Mercenaries looking for work meet in Virgin's Square. Stolen property can be fenced at the Undertark Tavern, which contains a secret entrance to Undermountain. Caravan Court is where caravans and their guards muster. The House of Song, guildhall of the Council of Musicians, Instrument-Makers, & Choristers, offers hospitality to itinerant bards. The Zoarstar, guildhall of the Scriveners', Scribes', & Clerks' Guild, boasts a vast collection of maps, almanacs and guides to all Toril.

280.content:
Wealthy, mercantile, oligarchic Tashluta spreads across the upper slope of the inner rim of the vast Tashalar Basin caldera. The caldera is partially flooded by the Shining Sea, forming a natural harbor that protects the fleet of Rundeen ships that guards the port. Because of Tashalar's conflict with the yuan-ti, residents kill all reptiles in the city on sight.
Mummy lord Valin Sarnaster has taken up residence in the House of the All-Seeing Orb.

281.content: A Guild Arcane is a mages' guild in a Calishite city that controls and regulates all magic use in the city, governed by a caleph arcane.

282.content: Amlakkar are the city watch in Calishite cities. Amlakkar are indentured servants. Each amlak is equipped with a scimitar, spear, longbow, dagger, and net.

283.content: Ubtao is the patron deity of Chult and Founder of Mezro. Also known as the Father of the Dinosaurs, Ubtao is an aloof, detached primordial deity. Ubtao can appear in the form of a powerful male tabaxi or massive tyrannosaurus rex. Ubtao's dark antithesis is Eshowdow, the Shadow Giant. Together with Thard Harr, Ubtao opposes the snake god Sseth and his yuan-ti, who seek to enslave the tabaxi and wild dwarves of Chult. Ubtao guards the prison of Dendar underneath the Peaks of Flame.

284.content: The Peaks of Flame are a volcanic mountain range in Chult, Dendar the Night Serpent is imprisoned beneath the Peaks of Flame. Legends tell that Dendar's escape signals the end of the world.

285.content: Dendar the Night Serpent is a colossal serpent who devours nightmares and fears, plotting to bring about the end of the world. Some say Dendar is imprisoned under the Peaks of Flame.

286.content:
Calimport, vast metropolis on the edge of the Calim Desert, sprawls along the banks of the Calim River and the shores of the Shining Sea. It is a vast maze of narrow mud-brick alleys and stone passages between walled districts called drudachs.
Poor Shackles Ward is a fetid, burgeoning warren of huts and tents home to the Flesh Market, Slaver’s Guild, brothels, gambling halls and opium-den taverns.
Beneath Calimport extends the subterranean Muzad, undercity vice, shadow and terror.
Calimport's harbor is the largest in all Faerûn.
The amlakkar guards put down slave revolts but turn a blind eye to the black market in magical goods.
The practice of magic in Calimport is tightly controlled by the Guild Arcane, whose massive minaret headquarters, the Auret, towers over the Wizard Ward.
Rumors say that the Dendar-worshipping cult of the Sacred Order of Akabar has a cell in the Muzad.

287.content: An elder brain is the final stage of the mind flayer life cycle, a disembodied brain that lives in a brine-filled pool in a mind flayer city, filling its followers with dark dreams of illithid dominion.

288.content: The Absolute is a mysterious entity worshiped by Cult of the Absolute. Commonly believed by its worshipers to be a deity, the Absolute is rumored to be an enslaved elder brain. The Absolute's secret goal is to raise an army of illithids and telepathic cultists to conquer the Sword Coast.

289.content: Moonrise Towers is a former elven estate in the Western Heartlands converted into a dark stronghold of the Cult of the Absolute.

290.content: The Cult of the Absolute is a sect that worships a mysterious entity known as the Absolute. High-ranking True Souls use the telepathic abilities granted by the modified mindflayer tadpoles implanted in them to control lower-ranking Absolutists. The Cult of the Absolute has a secret stronghold at Moonrise Towers.

291.content:
The wild, rugged Western Heartlands contain the Backlands, an untamed frontier plagued by reaving goblinoid raiders, the secret, mythal-infused elven city of Evereska, the theocracy of Elturgard, inhabited by devout followers of Torm, the Loyal Fury, and defended by the paladin Order of the Companion, and Najara, the Kingdom of Serpents, comprised of nagas, yuan-ti, lizardfolk and other scalykind, ruled by King Jarant of the Serpentfolk from the underground capital at Ss'khanaja. Baldur's Gate is located in the Western Heartlands.
The Cult of the Absolute has a growing presence in the region in Baldur's Gate and at Moonrise Towers.



The wild, rugged Western Heartlands contain the Backlands, an untamed frontier plagued by reaving goblinoid raiders, the secret, mythal-infused elven city of Evereska, the theocracy of Elturgard, inhabited by devout followers of Torm, the Loyal Fury, and defended by the paladin Order of the Companion, and Najara, the Kingdom of Serpents, comprised of nagas, yuan-ti, lizardfolk and other scalykind, ruled by King Jarant of the Serpentfolk from the underground capital at Ss'khanaja.
Baldur's Gate, the largest city in all Faerûn, is located in the Western Heartlands.

292.content: The Flaming Fist is a mercenary company that serves as city guards in Baldur's Gate as well as the city-state's military-expeditionary force. The Flaming Fist is a powerful organization, motivated by wealth and glory, but also focused on maintaining order throughout the Realms. At the top of the Flaming Fist's strict hierarchy is Grand Duke Ulder Ravengard, followed by Marshals, Blazes, Flames, Manips, Gauntlets and Fists (rank-and-file soldiers). The Flaming Fist often clashes with rival mercenary company the Zhentarim and the Cult of the Dragon.

293.comment: the Outer City of Baldur's Gate
293.content:
The Outer City of Baldur's Gate is a poor, lawless district outside the walls, a jumbled sprawl of huts, lean-tos, paddocks, stables and shacks where tanners, butchers and fabric dyers ply their trades and beggars, refugees and undesirables trudge through the muddy roads. The only semblance of order is enforced by the criminal organization known as the Guild. Demi-humans cluster in separate enclaves such as Stonyeyes, home to half-orcs, and Whitkeep, a neighborhood of gnomes, while Rivington is the domain of a contraband-smuggling gang called the Rivington Rats. The cult-infested Twin Songs district of the Outer City is a warren of small temples, hidden shrines and mysterious alley-altars sacred to dark, malevolent divinities.
Cultists of the Dead Three are on a murder spree.

294.content: The Avowed are cloistered monks, clerics and wizards who tend to the library-fortress of Candlekeep. The Avowed hire adventurers to search for long-lost items of lore, offering access to their archives of maps of treasure-filled ruins, documents explaining how to create magical items or scrolls with specifications for rare spells.

295.content:
Kolat Towers is a wizard's manor in Waterdeep. Though it is crumbling and seemingly abandoned, a magical wall of force surrounds the property's stone wall, keeping out would-be intruders.
Though it is rumored to be haunted, Kolat Towers has been occupied by a clone of Manshoon, the founder of the Zhentarim. The Towers' former owner, the late wizard Duhlark Kolat, has been turned into a flameskull that attacks trespassers.

296.content:
The Protector's Enclave is a district of Neverwinter home to Castle Never, stronghold of Lord Protector Neverember, who enjoys staunch support among its residents.
The festhall and tavern Moonstone Mask is located an earthmote suspended in the sky over the Protector's Enclave.
Rumor has it that agents of the Zhentarim and of the Xanathar's Thieves' Guild both plan to kidnap Renaer Neverember as they believe he knows how to use the Stone of Golorr.

297.content:
Candlekeep, bastion of magical knowledge, is a renowned library-fortress on the Sword Coast. Its soaring stone towers rise from a rocky promontory that juts into the Sea of Swords. It is the domain of the Avowed, monks of all planes of existence and races. Devotees of the seer Alaundo and his prophecies, their mission is to preserve knowledge and destroy the enemies of wisdom.
Inside Candlekeep's imposing front gates is the Court of Air, a vast cobbled plaza containing various shops and taverns, including the Hearth, the grand eating hall where Avowed mingle with Seekers.
An entrance-gift is required to pass into the Inner Ward and peruse the endless halls of the Great Library or enter the vaults and confer with the ghosts of sages of ages past.
The word of Keeper of the Tomes Janussi is considered law within Candlekeep.
The saprophytic plague has broken out in the Sword Coast, causing disease and famine.



Candlekeep is a renowned library-fortress and bastion of learning that stands on a rocky promontory jutting into the Sea of Swords. The keep is the domain of the Avowed, monks whose mission is to preserve knowledge and destroy the enemies of wisdom.

298.content:
The Sword Coast is a vast wilderness along the Sea of Swords overrun by bands of monstrous creatures and traversed by the Coast Way. The teeming metropolitan port-city of Baldur's Gate is a major trade hub and stronghold of the Lords' Alliance. Landmarks include Warlock's Crypt, den of the lich Larloch, Lizard Marsh, the Troll Hills, Cloak Wood, the terrifying ruins of Dragonspear Castle, and the ruined Ulcaster School of Wizardry, haunted by its founder, the conjurer Ulcaster.
The saprophytic plague has broken out in the Sword Coast, causing disease and famine.



The Sword Coast is a vast wilderness along the Sea of Swords overrun by bands of monstrous creatures and traversed by the Coast Way. The teeming metropolitan port-city of Baldur's Gate is a major trade hub and stronghold of the Lords' Alliance. Landmarks include Warlock's Crypt, den of the lich Larloch, Lizard Marsh, the Troll Hills, Cloak Wood, the terrifying ruins of Dragonspear Castle, and the ruined Ulcaster School of Wizardry, haunted by its founder, the conjurer Ulcaster.

299.content: The saprophytic plague is a supernatural fungal disease spread by spores emitted by the infected. Its first symptom is fever, followed by oozing lesions. Victims then become mindless, zombie-like creatures. In the final stage of saphrophytic plague, the victim's body dissolves into an intelligent magenta ooze.

300.content: The Stone of Golorr is an artifact that contains the consciousness of the aboleth Golorr. It is rumored to have been stolen by the Xanathar.

301.content: The Auret is the headquarters of the Guild Arcane in Calimport. The Auret is a towering minaret of solid gold, its walls seeming to writhe with ever-shifting arcane symbols. The Auret has no permanent doors, its walls instead magically opening to admit guild members.

302.content: A canopic golem is a large crystalline construct made using the organs of the living.

303.comment: the Spine of the World range
303.content:
The Spine of the World is a craggy, nigh-impassable mountain range known as "the Wall" that protects Faerûn from the far-north arctic expanse of the Endless Ice Sea.
The Spine is contended by the dwarves of fabled Mithral Hall, which extends beneath Fourthpeak Mountain, the Skortchclaw orcs under Ugra Ngarl, who have seized the fallen dwarven Fortress Eyegad, the duergars of Clan Sunblight, who hold the cliffside fortress of Sunblight, and the frost giants of Tholvarr.
Wealthy mining city Mirabar lies at the foot of the Spine of the World range. Ancient evil red dragon Klauth is said to still lair in the Klauthen Vale to the west of Mirabar, where he welcomes a growing presence of the Cult of the Dragon.



The Spine of the World is a craggy, nigh-impassable mountain range known as "the Wall" that protects Faerûn from the far-north arctic expanse of the Endless Ice Sea.
The vast mineral wealth of the Spine, extracted daily from the deep mines of ore-rich Mirabar, is contended by the dwarves of fabled Mithral Hall, which extends beneath Fourthpeak Mountain, the Skortchclaw orcs under Ugra Ngarl, who have seized the fallen dwarven Fortress Eyegad, and the duergars of Clan Sunblight, who hold the cliffside fortress of Sunblight, and the frost giants of Tholvarr.

304.content: Xxiphu, the Soaring City, is an ancient mobile aboleth city that hovers over the Sea of Fallen Stars near Akanûl. Xxiphu is a floating glyph-inscribed obelisk with tentacles extending from its walls, lashed by an eternal storm. The glyphs depict thousands of constantly changing images, too alien for mortal minds to comprehend. Reality is altered near Xxiphu, spawning aberrations. Xxiphu is home to the Abolethic Sovereignty.

305.content:
The World Serpent Inn is a celebrated meeting point of several planes.
The common room has plank floors, flagstone fireplaces and glowing fluted pillars. A blue mist renders the room hazy and indistinct. In the middle, a large oak bar stands in a shaft of light. There are no windows. A massive brawling pit occupies one side of the common room.
The Inn’s wine cellar is its own plane, governed by a deity of alcohol. The Inn’s back rooms are a labyrinth of corridors with shifting portals to various planes.
The Inn’s positive magical energy boosts healing and friendship. It is neutral ground, with fighting only in the pit.
Exotic drinks: elven zzar, orc-brewed oxblood ale, Elysium elixir, Sigma flytrapper, Sterozium, Styx Sorrows.
The Inn’s barkeep, Mitchifer, cannot control the front door portals; only the enigmatic Owner, possibly an overgod, can change the Inn’s planar alignment.
The tiny serpent wench gnomish waitresses hoist heavy tankards with ease.



The World Serpent Inn is a mysterious drinking establishment located where several planes meet; that meeting point shifts, frequented by exotic creatures and races from all worlds and even the odd deity. Patrons at the Inn never know what the night will bring or whether the portal they stumbled in through will lead to the same world when they stumble back out.

306.content:
The Church of Bhaal is a cabal of evil priests and assassins who worship the Lord of Murder. Bhaalists meticulously research targets, execute assassinations, hunt bounties and commit holy ritual murder. Bhaalist temples are often hidden underground beneath cities. Bhaalists view murder as a pleasure, as well as a means of strengthening their master, and make sure their victims know the Lord of Murder is behind their killing. Bhaalists must murder regularly: once every tenday, during the darkest time of the night.



The Church of Bhaal is a cabal of evil priests and assassins who worship the Lord of Murder.

307.content:
The Red Wizards of Thay are undead arcanist agents of dread lich and supreme regent Szass Tam. The Red Wizards expand the influence of Thay through raids on the bordering wild lands of Rashemen and Aglarond or expeditions in search of magical artifacts. Red Wizards travel protected by gladiators of Thay, clerics of Kossuth or Thayan knights.



The Red Wizards of Thay are agents of dread lich and supreme regent Szass Tam tasked with expanding the influence of Thay throughout Faerûn.

308.content: The Rundeen are a slaving and mercantile consortium based in the Sword Coast and Chult. The Rundeen seek profit above all else, using their vast network to send local goods to far-off corners of Faerûn. The Rundeen hire pirates and brigands to attack rival traders and recruit promising merchants to become affiliates, offering benefits in exchange for a portion of profits. The Rundeen are arch-enemies of the Harpers and consider eliminating Harpist agents a high priority. The Rundeen are allied with the Knights of the Shield and the yuan-ti of Tashalar.

309.content: Dock Ward contains the Great Harbor of Waterdeep, shipbuilding yards and warehouses. They say mermaids, sirens and selkies live in the harbor, and some of them even work at The Blushing Mermaid, Dock Ward's most luxurious establishment. The Black Boar Tribe gang operates from Dock Ward. The Shard Shunners, a gang of halfling wererats, also have their hideout in in Dock Ward. The Grey Hands are investigating a rumor that a friendly bronze dragon named Zelifarn has made its lair in a hidden underwater sea-cave. Strange lights have been seen at night in the windows of the abandoned Kolat Towers.

310.content: The Blushing Mermaid is a luxurious tavern and inn in Waterdeep's Dock Ward. It offers a heated bathhouse where patrons soak in scented water as they dine, served by mermaids, who swim in from the harbor via secret tunnels. The Blushing Mermaid's proprietress, Lady Alathene Moonstar, uses magic to keep up her beauty despite her great age. As a game, each night all lights in the Blushing Mermaid are magically extinguished and the tipsy patrons must grope their way in the darkness. Some whisper that guests vanish from the Mermaid. These rumors mention a circular staircase rising from the central mermaid pool hall to a rooftop garden with bones bound to its rails. They say Lady Moonstar is an archlich whose unlife enchantments are failing and who is thus forced to maintain her youthful appearance by draining the lives of hapless guests.

311.content: The Northdark is an underground domain of the Underdark. The Northdark contains the svirfneblin city of Blingdenstone, the duergar deepkingdom of Gracklstugh and the drow cities of Menzoberranzan and Ched Nasad. Numerous crumbled ancient realms were also found in the Northdark, such as Ammarindar, Delzoun and Netheril, in the form of Skullport.

312.content:
Beneath Baldur's Gate lies a sleazy underground tavern and festhall known as the Undercellar, situated in a series of dank cellars, twisting corridors and cramped tunnels that run beneath the Upper City. Baldurians like to visit the Undercellar incognito, wearing masks to conceal their identities while they get up to the sort of drunken debauchery frowned upon topside. Entrances into the secretive Undercellar are controlled by criminals or merchants. 
Deeper down, below the Undercellar, lie tunnels and caves containing the ruins of an ancient settlement known as the Undercity, infested by undead and home to an old temple of Bhaal. Further down still, the tunnels connect to the Underdark.

313.content: The Bedine are nomadic, tent-dwelling, camel-herding desert tribesmen led by a sheikh. Distrustful of outsiders and honor-bound, Bedine are fiercely independent and resentful of foreign interference in their homeland of Anauroch. Bedine are superstitious and fearful of all things magical.

314.content: Phaerimm are malevolent, intelligent slug-like aberrations with incredibly powerful spellcasting abilities. They have flat heads dominated by a gaping maw rimmed with barbed teeth and venomous stingers on their tails. Their spiked, slug-shaped bodies are covered by a greenish scaly hide and their four arms are strong and dexterous. Phaerimm wield powerful mind-control magic that drains moisture from the desert. Phaerimm have a retinue of thralls of other races, which act as their servants and agents. They communicate telepathically through wind-whispering. Phaerimm make their lairs in fortified, warded caves.

315.content: At the dawn of time, in the Days of Thunder, vast empires of brutal reptilian, amphibian, and avian beings — aearee, batrachi, fey and sarrukh — dominated the world, building up towering cities of glass and stone joined by shining road, tamed the great dinosaurs and experimented with unrefined wild magic, wielding powers that rival gods. Yet they waged endless wars of mutual hatred, their mages launching blasts that annihilated armies and mountains, causing a cataclysm that led to their downfall. Little remains from those ancient times, and perhaps it is for the best.

316.content: Pterafolk are a race of shape-shifting pteranodon-like humanoids native to the jungles of Chult. In their natural form pterafolk are tall reptilian humanoids with cranial crests, smooth scales, thin limbs and sharp claws. They are violent and xenophobic. They can shapeshift into leathery-winged pteranodons and favor dive-bombing tactics in battle. Pterafolk tribes are often led by a spirit naga chieftain.

317.content: Earthwood is a dense forest in the Earthspur Mountains within Damara, where the birch and evergreen trees grow quickly due to the magic of a druid attempting to stop the advance of the Great Glacier.

318.content: A phylactery is a rare, expensive magical item that holds the life force of a lich. A person who can find where a lich has hidden their phylactery can destroy the lich by destroying the phylactery or use the phylactery to gain control of the lich. Each phylactery is unique and it takes great magical knowledge and skill to identify the form of defense and means of destruction of a phylactery. A phylactery can take any form, but common forms include a metal box, ring, amulet, gem, or doll.

319.content:
The crystal shard Crenshinibon is an evil sentient relic of immense power, obsessed with dominion and control and utterly without scruples. Crenshinobon manipulates and corrupts its wielder with promises of power, turning its master into its slave. The weak-minded hark to the crystal's siren call, forming an army that mindlessly obeys the crystal's master.
Crenshinibon creates a crystalline tower, Cryshal-Tirith, as its stronghold.

320.content:
Aglarond is a magocratic nation with its capital at Veltalar ruled by the Simbarchs. The Stone Bears are notorious thieves led by revolutionary Ambal scheming to overthrow the Simbarchs. Fey-dominated Yuirwood, home to star elves resentful of Simbarch rule, is tainted by plaguelands and contains the Sunglade, a Seldarine menhir circle with portals to the Feywild. The magically engineered Watchwall protects Aglarond against incursions by the lich and necromancer lords of neighboring Thay. Adventurers out of Citadel Dantalien raid Undumor, fortress occupied by Thayan vampire knights. Off the coast of Aglarond, beneath the Sea of Fallen Stars, sea monsters guard the sunken treasures of the lost city of Laothkund the Drowned.

Adventurers out of Citadel Dantalien raid Undumor, fortress occupied by Thayan vampire knights. Off the coast of Aglarond, beneath the Sea of Fallen Stars, sea monsters guard the sunken treasures of the lost city of Laothkund the Drowned.

321.content: The Simbarchs of Aglrarond are powerful wizards, former apprentices of the vanished Simbul. The Simbarchs rule Aglarond through the Simbarch Council. Compassionate and restrained, Simbarchs are masters of silver fire magic. Simbarchs have been known to go adventuring in defense of Aglarond.

322.content: The Simbul, born Alassra Shentrantra Silverhand, and also known as the Witch-Queen, is one of the Seven Sisters, a Chosen of Mystra, a former ruler of Aglarond and one of the most powerful spellcasters in Faerûn. A staunch opponent of Thay, the Simbul is widely believed to have perished in battle, though rumors continue to tell of sightings of the great Witch-Queen.

323.content: The Watchwall is a colossal, magically engineered stone wall protecting Aglarond. The Watchwall runs from the fortress city of Glarondar to the slopes of Mount Umbergoth. The Watchwall overlooks the monster-infested mudflats of the Umber Marshes. The Watchwall's undermanned garrison, the Army of the Green Drake, stationed at Glarond Keep, struggles to guard the Watchwall's great length from incursions from Thay and the Umber Marshes.

324.content: Undumor is a dread fortress-city in Aglarond. Undumor is occupied by vampiric knights of Thay commanded by Red Wizard necromancers under governor Ruralekh Prator, a conjurer capable of summoning an army of behirs, chimeras, and ropers.

325.content: Citadel Dantalien is a massive fortress constructed by the Simbarchs of Aglarond to defend against the undead forces occupying Undumor. Citadel Dantalien lies directly across the wide Umber River from Undumor. The citadel provides training and equipment to recruits and sends adventurers on missions to Undumor. It is rumored that the undead armies of Undumor have been digging tunnels for some nefarious purpose.

326.content:
Akanûl is a magically jumbled land of rock spires and floating earthmotes, home to the Underchasm and the Glass Mesa, a forbidden mountain of quartz. Elemental energy lashes Akanûl with chaotic magical storms. Akanûl is governed by the genasi of the floating city of Airspur, ruled by Queen Arathane and the Four Stewards. Ravenous aboleths stalk the southern skies from their base at Xxiphu, the floating monolith city. The treasure-rich ruins of Chondathan cities draw adventurers to ravines infested by predators from Abeir. The rebel genasi of the Firestorm Cabal occupy the floating fortress of Brassune Safehold, a forestmote overlooking the ruins of Brassune, occupied by the kuo-toa minions of the Abolethic Sovereignty. A mysterious elder gray dragon is said to lair in Dragonroost, hidden among the Akanapeaks.



Akanûl, magically transposed in the Spellplague, is an irregular jumble of jutting spires, jagged ravines, floating earthmotes and watermotes bordering the Underchasm, punctuated by the Glass Mesa, a forbidden mountain of transparent quartz. The elemental energy coursing through Akanûl causes chaotic weather patterns. Akanûl is governed by the genasi of the glittering floating city of of Airspur, ruled by Queen Arathane and the Four Stewards of Earth, Fire, Sky and Sea.

327.content: The Glass Mesa is a mysterious mountain of translucent quartz that juts from Akanûl. It is strictly forbidden to approach or touch the Glass Mesa. The edict prohibiting entry to Glass Mesa is enforced on pain of death by genasi forces based in Airspur.

328.content:
Airspur is an aerial city of genasi in Akanûl. Airspur's elemental spires stand on floating earthmotes linked by bridges. Airspur is ruled by Queen Arathane and her genasi council of the Four Stewards and defended by the drake-riding windsoul genasi of the Sky Guard. The Firestorm Cabal have a chapter house in the city and perform secret missions on behalf of the queen. The finest drakes in all Faerûn can be purchased in Airspur's Drakeyards. The aerial couriers of the Airsteppers Guild can deliver a message anywhere.



Airspur is an aerial city of genasi in Akanûl. Airspur's elemental spires stand on floating earthmotes linked by bridges. Airspur is ruled by Queen Arathane and her genasi council of the Four Stewards and defended by the drake-riding windsoul genasi of the Sky Guard. The Firestorm Cabal have a chapter house in the city and perform secret missions on behalf of the queen. The finest drakes in all Faerûn can be purchased in Airspur's Drakeyards.

329.content:
A stormsoul genasi has an elemental connection to storms. Stormsoul genasi have purple skin etched with silver szuldar lines of energy and glowing, crystal spikes of silver instead of hair.



A stormsoul genasi is a genasi with an elemental connection to storms. Stormsoul genasi have purple skin etched with silver szuldar lines of energy and glowing, crystal spikes of silver instead of hair.

330.content: The Merchants' Ward of Port Nyanzaru is a wealthy district of grand villa estates home to the city's merchant princes. Merchants' Ward occupies the slopes of Temple Hill, resplendent with the temples of Gond, Savras and Sund, and Throne Hill, crowned by stately Goldenthrone, the palace where the merchant princes gather to deliberate and hold audience. Merchants' Ward also contains the Grand Souk, a sprawling covered marketplace, and the famous Jewel Market.

331.content: Tiamat is the evil dragon goddess of greed and queen of evil chromatic dragons. Tiamat is the eternal rival of her brother Bahamut, ruler of the good metallic dragons. Tiamat can appear as a five-headed chromatic dragon or as her avatar, the Dark Lady, a mulan woman with all-black eyes and a seductive smile. Arrogant, vain and manipulatively disdainful of mortals, Tiamat never forgets a slight and is focused on gaining wealth and power. Her lair is the Dragonspawn Pits of Azharul in the Dragon Eyrie. Through her Church and the Cult of the Dragon, Tiamat seeks to take over the realms, and particularly Unther, Chessenta, Murghôm, Tymanther and the dragon empires of Laerakond.

332.content: Selpir is an enclave of linked stone towers in Nembral where the reclusive Lords of Nimbral live. Selpir is a vast warren of many linked living spaces, pantries, spell workshops, and storage rooms, defended by golems and other constructs, and by wards that detect -- and can forcibly teleport -- intruders. The skyships that brought the Voyagers to Nimbral are built into its towers, but are now dormant.

333.content:
The Nimbral Lords rule Sea Haven through their Heralds and Knights from Selpir. The Lords have amassed great power in illusion magic. They have intermarried for generations and live as one big, eccentric family. They guard their isolation and secrecy, lest jealous magic users like the Red Wizards of Thay seek to steal their superior arcane knowledge. The Lords have many fighting constructs, magic items like the staff of cosmos and spells for scrying from afar, detecting active spells and magic items in Nimbral and protecting Lords' minds from magic. In the event of magical intruders, the Lords assume the magical disguise of hermits. If an intruder attacks with magic, they are teleported to the dungeons of Starshot to convince them that the Lords are dead or gone mad in the magic ruins.
The current elders are Elders are as follows: the motherly Ardanthe, sharp-tongued Skouloun, taciturn, pensive Mardamaun, impish Yusendre and elderly, kindly, manipulative Belaurant.

334.content: The Council of Lords is the governing body of the Lords’ Alliance. The current members of the Council of Lords are Laeral Silverhand, Open Lord of Waterdeep, Dagult Neverember, Lord Protector of Neverwinter, Taern Hornblade, High Mage of Silverymoon, Ulder Ravengard, Grand Duke of Baldur’s Gate and Marshal of the Flaming Fist, Morwen Daggerford, Duchess of Daggerford, Selin Ramur, Marchion of Mirabar, Dowell Harpell of Longsaddle, Dagnabbet Waybeard, Queen of Mithral Hall, Lord Dauner Ilzimmer of Amphail, and Nestra Ruthiol, Waterbaron of Yartar.

335.content:
Mantol-Derith is a trading post, caravan stop and tent city in the Underdark. It lines the shores of Darklake, on the far side from the duergar city of Gracklstugh. Dark water rushes beneath its bridges, carved from crystal, and the cave walls glow and sparkle. Campsites of drow, illithid, svirfneblin, and duergar merchants and bugbear mercenaries sprawl across the cave floor.
The stalls of Mantol-Derith's Central Market are tucked away beneath giant fungi. Its only public establishment, the Nameless Inn, is run by a cynical, sharp-tongued duergar woman named Dinnika and staffed by inept and impertinent goblin slave-girls. Famed for its mushroom ale, the recipe for which Dinnika is said to have killed to protect, the Inn offers cozy if sparsely furnished rooms in private grottoes.
Massive warehouse storage areas occupy the four corners of the cavern, each claimed by one of Mantol-Derith's four factions: drow, duergar, svirfneblin, and Zhentarim.



Mantol-Derith is a trading city in a cavern in the Underdark on the shores of Darklake, on the far side from the duergar city of Gracklstugh. The cavern of Mantol-Derith is full of waterfalls, pools, and streams crossed by bridges carved from crystal, its walls lined with multicolored crystals and gems. The city is made up largely of caravans and campsites of drow, illithid, svirfneblin, and duergar merchants and bugbear mercenaries. 
The Central Market of Mantol-Derith is ringed with giant fungi, beneath which are stalls selling fruit, perfume, woods, and spices.
The Nameless Inn is run by a duergar woman named Dinnika who keeps goblin slaves. The Inn is known for its mushroom ale. Its rooms are located in crevices behind petrified mushroom doors.
There are four huge warehouse storage areas in Mantol-Derith at the four corners of the cavern, one for each of the city’s factions.

336.content: The Darklake is a series of underground bodies of water in the Underdark connected by locks. Gracklstugh, Mantol-Derith and Sloobludop stand on its shores. The Darklake is located in a huge cavern that takes two days to cross by boat. Stalagmites, stalactites, and columns jut from its surface. Duergar from Gracklstugh patrol the Darklake.

337.content: Gracklstugh is a duergar metropolis on the shores of the Darklake in the Northdark section of the Underdark.

338.content: The Labyrinth is an ancient maze of tunnels in the Northdark section of the Underdark.

339.content:
Grimlocks are blind, eyeless humanoids that live in the Underdark, the degenerated descendants of humans. They have sharp teeth, decorative scarification, mottled, grey scales, claw-like nails and unkempt hair. Grimlocks rely on a strong sense of smell and echolocation to perceive their environment without sight. They fight savagely with bone or stone clubs and axes and drool over human flesh, which they tear raw from the bone. Grimlocks are xenophobic, withdrawn creatures who roam in small hunting packs.

They have sharp teeth, decorative scarification and mottled, grey scales, claw-like nails and unkempt hair. Grimlocks rely on a strong sense of smell and echolocation to perceive their environment without sight. They fight savagely with bone or stone clubs and axes and drool over human flesh, which they tear raw from the bone. Grimlocks are xenophobic, withdrawn creatures who roam in small hunting packs.

340.content: The Triceratops Society, also known as the Ytepka Society, is a secret society of tabaxi that protects Chult from foreigners. The Ytepka spy on and take clandestine action against foreign groups in Chult: brigands, pirates explorers, adventurers and mercenaries. The Triceratops Society is locked in conflict with the Children of the Ebon Hand, religious zealots of Eshowdow who seek to destroy the tabaxi. The Merchant Princes of Port Nyanzaru entrust the Society with secret missions to protect the city against foreign powers from outside Chult.

341.content:
Port Nyanzaru is a mercantile city-state in Chult. Each of Nyanzaru's seven merchant princes controls a domain of trade: Ekene-Afa weapons, Ifan Talro'a dinosaurs and flying monkeys, Jessamine poisons and writs of assassination, Jobal jungle guide and mercenary services, Kwayothé alcohol, insect repellent and perfume, Wakanga O'tamu lore and magic items and Zhanthi jewelry and armor. The secretive Triceratops Society protects Chult against imperialist foreigners, such as the Flaming Fist mercenaries based at Fort Beluarian. Port Nyanzaru is divided into Merchants' Ward, Harbor Ward and Market Ward, and the slum districts of Old City, Malar's Throat and Tiryki Anchorage. Criminals may find that a writ of assassination (murder permit) has been issued against them or even be tossed into the beast pit at Executioner's Run. Dragon turtle Aremag has been sighted in the bay, the vegepygmy presence in the jungle is growing and the pirates are raiding closer to Fort Nyanzaru.

342.content:
Verdans are goblinoids with telepathic abilities subject to frequent mutations of size, skin color, and physical traits. The physical fluidity of verdans leads them to attach little importance to appearance and to champion diversity and freedom, fighting oppression in all forms. Verdans tend to roam the world in search of new experiences, adopting new identities as their bodies continue to molt and reform.



Verdans are goblinoids with telepathic abilities who undergo frequent mutations. Verdans attach little importance to appearance and champion diversity and freedom, fighting oppression in all forms as they roam the world in search of new experiences and new identities.

343.content:
The Harbor Ward of Port Nyanzaru houses the city's docks, including the Royal Docks of its merchant princes. Dinosaurs pull ships through canals and dinosaur-powered cranes unload goods.
Fort Nyanzaru guards the port against pirates with its great chain that can be raised across the harbor to stop ships.
A bulletin board outside the Harbormaster’s Office advertises wilderness guides the Chultan jungles.
A network of caves, said to contain an old temple to Umberlee, lies beneath the streets.

344.content: Plaguelands are places where wild magic runs amok, causing mutations into plaguenchanged or plaguescarred creatures. Plaguelands are shrouded in luminous, blue fog, the land within mutable, like boiling mud. Earthmotes and zones of blue fire are common in plaguelands, where reality is in flux, forming an alien landscape.

345.content:
Targos is a fishing village in the Ten Towns region of Frozenfar. Its walls protect it against orcs and other threats from the wilderness, but can do little to keep out the Frostmaiden's unending chill: the perpetual winter has frozen the town's harbor, making life a struggle for the town's trout fishermen. Speaker Naerth Maxildanarr is a shady character with reputed ties to the Zhentarim and a secret network of spies throughout the Ten Towns. As long as he keeps the money flowing into Targos, the hardbitten locals are willing to turn a blind eye to his crimes. From Targos, Bremen, Bryn Shander and Termalaine can be reached overland with appropriate winter gear.
The rat-infested, decrepit Luskan Arms Inn is the closest thing to a public establishment in Targos. Triglio's General Store sells fishing tackle, sailing gear, snowshoes and winter survival equipment.
A foolhardy adventuring party from Targos has gone missing on the slopes of the formidable Kelvin Cairn.

346.content: Veltalar is a port-city in Aglarond on the coast of the Sea of Fallen Stars. Veltalar has a large elf and half-elf population. Old Velprintalar is a slum created by the subsidence of the sea, which left its old port dry and hence useless. The abandoned old city's squalor makes it a hotbed for Stone Bears, who commit daring heists to fund their efforts to unseat the Simbarchs, whom they portray as magitocratic tyrants. The wizards of the Simbarch Council meet in the refined, arcane retreat of the former Palace of the Simbul. In the taverns and plazas of Veltalar, recruiters seek adventurers to man the Watchwall and aid the troops at Citadel Dantalien with the siege of Undumor.

347.content:
Elder runes are commonly understood ancient glyphs used as signs of warning or notice for travelers. The elder runes are Anarath, Angras, Bairemuth, Gatha, Ingolth, Korombos,
Laebos, Lammath, Nchasme, Qualos, Retniw, Savaros, Tergara
Ullathar, Uttebyn, Vakaros.

348.content: Rune types include Harper's marks, elder runes and mage runes.

349.content: Anarath is the elder rune for marking a guardian.

350.content: Angras is the elder rune for marking danger or war.

351.content: Bairemuth is the elder rune for marking a place of death.

352.content: Gatha is the elder rune for marking magic, fey, or entities from another plane of existence.

353.content: Korombos is the elder rune for marking a place of chaos.

354.content: Laebos is the elder rune for marking fire.

355.content: Mage sigils, also known as mage runes, are sigils used by wizards to mark their possessions, sign their names or associate something with themselves. Sigils are often triggers for magical spells, such as symbol spells, explosive runes, fire traps and glyphs of warding.

356.content:
Auril is the goddess of winter and cold. She embodies winter's cruelty in all its deadliest aspects, and has a heart of ice to match her fatally cold beauty, eternally preserved beneath a sheet of rime.
As the Frostmaiden, she is a lithe, attractive woman with blue skin, a body of ice and snow, free-flowing white hair and frost swirling around her.
Arrogant, vain, cruel, and capricious, Auril is cold and unfeeling, save for her lone obsession with using ice to freeze and thus preserve all forms of beauty, from nature to art and the artists themselves. The Frostmaiden's ultimate goal is to cover all the Realms in ice and snow.

357.content:
Frozenfar is a frigid, remote northern region home to the frontier villages known as Ten Towns in the tundra of Icewind Dale, the jagged, impassable Spine of the World Mountains, which shield the civilized world against the horrors beyond, and the Sea of Moving Ice, an uncharted region of icebergs and floating islands.
Frozenfar is locked in an unnatural winter known as the Everlasting Rime, rumored to be the work of Auril the Frostmaiden. Blizzards, avalanches and freezing temperatures make travel dangerous and survival a challenge.



Frozenfar is a frigid, remote northern region home to the frontier villages known as Ten Towns in the tundra of Icewind Dale, the jagged, impassable Spine of the World Mountains, which shield the civilized world against the horrors beyond, and the Sea of Moving Ice, an uncharted region of icebergs and floating islands.

358.content:
Bryn Shander, largest of the Ten Towns, is a walled city on a windswept hill in Frozenfar. Perpetual winter has closed the roads and trade is suffering. Blackiron Blades is a small smithy run by Garn the Hammer and his sister Elza, who need help recovering supplies after a dogsled caravan carrying ingots got lost in a blizzard. House of the Morninglord is a Temple of Amaunator run by a retired adventurer named Mishann eager to discover why Auril is causing the Everlasting Rime. Speaker Duvessa Shane and Sheriff Markham Southwell struggle to maintain order in Bryn Shander as residents scheme to avoid being selected as the next human sacrifice to appease the Frostmaiden. Scramsax's Northlook Tavern is where mercenaries and adventurers go to find work.
From Bryn Shander travelers can each Targos, Termalaine, Good Mead, Easthaven and Caer-Dineval, though snowshoes and heavy winter clothing or dogsleds will be required to survive the trek.

359.content:
Ship Kurth is one of five pirate gangs that control turf in the ruined city of Luskan. Ship Kurth is led by High Captain Beniago Kurth. The gang runs a tavern on the Northern Bank called One-Eyed Jax.
Ship Kurth has its headquarters in a fortified tower on Closeguard Island in Luskan's River Mirar estuary.

360.content:
Luskan is a lawless, dilapidated port city and cove of pirates and smugglers dominated by pirate gangs known as the Ships of the High Captains.
Over Luskan looms the Host Tower of the Arcane, whose eerie branchlike spires are home to a resurgent Arcane Brotherhood.
Luskan is a dangerous place. Kobolds and cultists squat in its abandoned buildings, and the boglike estuary of the River Mirar is infested with aquatic monstrosities.
Everything from slaves to Netherese artifacts can be had in Luskan's black markets.
The drow mercenaries of Bregan D'aerthe have a stronghold in the ancient ruins of Luskan's Old Illusk quarter. Some say the dark elves have taken over Ship Kurth and rule the city using the gang as their human pawns.
Luskan is located in the Sword Coast North, at the mouth of the swampy River Mirar, which divides the city into the districts of Northern Bank, Southern Bank and islands.
