361.content:
Warforged are self-aware, intelligent humanoid magical constructs with metal or stone bodies. Each warforged has a distinctive ghulra rune on their forehead. Warforged tend to have strong work ethics and pursue straightforward goals, but some question the nature of their consciousness and role in the world.



Warforged are self-aware, intelligent humanoid magical constructs with metal or stone bodies.

362.content: The Harpers are a secret society of spies, infiltrators and agents with safehouses throughout the Realms operating in the shadows with the mission of achieving fair, equal treatment for all. Goals: thwart tyrants and aid the weak, poor, and oppressed.

363.content:
Dragonborn are powerfully built draconic humanoids with reptilian anatomy, scaly skin, claws and the ability to use a breath weapon.



Dragonborn are draconic humanoids with reptilian anatomy, scaly skin, claws and the ability to use a breath weapon.

364.content:
Bregan D'aerthe is an elite drow mercenary and mercantile company founded and led by Jarlaxle. Its main base of operations is in the Clawrift in Menzoberranzan, and on the surface it has a major presence in Luskan and Calimport. In addition to fighting for the highest bidder, Bregan D'aerthe trades in rare surface goods and acts as an information broker, selling to whoever pays the most, without scruples.
In the surface world, the drow of Bregan d'aerthe often operate as clandestine agents, using magical disguises to walk among surface-dwellers unsuspected.

365.content:
The Church of Selûne is a female-dominated faith that worships and serves the goddess Selûne. Be they lay servitors, temple priests, itinerant clerics, silverstars, mystics or crusaders, Selûnites preach acceptance, tolerance, compassion, humility and self-reliance. The Church of Selûne wages holy war against evil in all its forms, and especially the Church of Shar, devotees of Selûne's evil sister.
Selûnite rituals include libations of milk and wine, transmuted into moonfire by a moonstone altar, and night stalk walks and dances in the light of the full moon, when Selûne is closest.
The most devout can commune with Selûne in visions through the Mystery of the Night or even take part in a Conjuring of the Second Moon, held every four years on on Shieldmeet, when Shards (planetar servants of Selûne) are summoned to fight the dark forces of Shar.



The Church of Selûne is a religious organization that worships and serves the goddess Selûne. Selûnites preach acceptance, tolerance, compassion, humility and self-reliance. The Church of Selûne wages holy war against evil in all its forms, and especially the Church of Shar, devotees of Selûne's evil sister.

366.content:
Chauntea is the benevolent goddess of life and bounty, embodying all things agrarian. Also known as the Earthmother, Chauntea is the patroness of agriculture and plant cultivation.
Chauntea opposes all those who desecrate and expunge nature. Chauntea's nemeisis is Talona, the Lady of Pestilence.

367.content:
The Three Black Rings is a drow merchant company that employs creatures of all races as caravan guards. The company seeks new, alternate routes through the Underdark, particularly from Skullport via the Labyrinth to the trading post of Mantol-Derith and the city of Menzoberranzan. Drow and half-drow are in command with surface-dwellers only in subordinate roles. As a drow company, the Three Black Rings is shunned and banned among respectable surface folk; still, many smugglers, mercenaries and thieves are happy to do business with the drow, purchasing exotic Underdark delicacies and selling slaves.



The Three Black Rings is a drow merchant company that employs creatures of all races as laborers and caravan guards. The clan seeks new, alternate routes through the Underdark, selling maps of these routes and hiring out guides to other merchants.

368.content: The Caer is a stout castle of plain, cold stone that stands on the cliff overlooking the town of Caer-Dineval and the frozen lake. Sinister figures in dark robes stand watch in the guardhouse overlooking the wooden doors at the front gatehouse, turning away any who present themselves at the gate. The robed figures wear sword-shaped crystal amulets that glow with a dull, menacing light.

369.content:
The Caer – the ancient fortress that gives the lakeside hamlet of Caer-Dineval its name – squats grimly on the cliff overlooking the harbor.
With the fishing port iced over and the snow choking the roads to Caer-Konig, life in Caer-Dineval under the Everlasting Rime is grim. Even the town's only tavern, the Uphill Climb, on the slope of the hill beneath the castle, has nothing left to drink now that the ice has shut down ferry to Good Mead, and only fish chowder to offer hungry visitors. The tavernkeep, Roark, has no rooms to rent, suggesting that that visitors seek shelter from the cold at the Caer, now the residence of Speaker Crannoc Siever.

370.content:
The lakeside town of Caer-Konig slumbers half-buried in snow at the foot of the mountain Kelvin's Cairn. A few splintered stakes from the old palisade still jut from the frozen ground. Low terraced houses ring the shore of the ice-choked harbor. On the hill above is a jagged heap of stones that was once the town's keep, long ago sacked by orcs.
Cut off from the other Ten Towns by the Everlasting Rime, Caer-Konig's residents get by on what they can fish out of the half-frozen lake. A rash of mysterious break-ins has been plaguing the town; inexplicably, the thieves have been taking jewelry, particularly crystal items, rather than food. The Hook, Line and Sinker Tavern offers a free mug of ale to newcomers and always has a drinking contest at closing time. After a few rounds, patrons swear that the thefts are the work of mysterious invisible figures, whose footprints always lead towards the slopes of Kelvin's Cairn.

371.content: A wemic is a creature with the upper body of a humanoid and the lower body of a lion.

372.content: Vaasa is a bleak region of tundra, moorlands and frozen wastes. Vaasa is a feudal society of serfs and slaves ruled by the Warlock Knights and landowning nobility called Fellthanes with absolute power over their fiefdoms. The Ironfell Council of Warlock Knights in the Grand Citadel of the Sky in Telos City organizes the defense of Vaasa against the Ring-nose orcs, the Garuk One Ears goblins, and the White Worm human barbarians.

373.content:
The Warlock Knights are the brutal, expansionist feudal lords and elite military force of Vaasa. They take their orders from the Ironfell Council and the Voice of Telos in the Citadel of the Iron Sky, Telos City. The Warlock Knights draw arcane power from a pact with the dormant primordial Telos. Their main goal is gaining power. At home in Vaasa, the Knights scheme for position with rival lords. Abroad, they manipulate proxies and launch direct attacks on their neighbors, especially Damara, the Moonsea and the giant kingdom of Kultaakarr.
In battle, the Knights use as front line combatants goblins, gnolls and viscous, suicidal constructs called shardsouls.



The Warlock Knights are the brutal, expansionist feudal lords and elite military force of Vaasa. They take their orders from the Ironfell Council and the Voice of Telos. The Warlock Knights draw arcane power from a pact with the dormant primordial Telos. Their main goal is gaining power. At home in Vaasa, the Knights scheme for position with rival lords. Abroad, they manipulate proxies and launch direct attacks on their neighbors, especially Damara, the Moonsea and the giant kingdom of Kultaakarr.

374.content: Bloodstone Pass is the only way through the Galena Mountains between Damara and Vaasa. The invading Warlock Knights have occupied the Vaasan gate and the ruins of Bloodstone City, while the defending Damarans hold the Damaran Gate.

375.content:
The Moonsea Lands are a harsh, cold northern frontier made up of the blizzard-prone, ore-rich Dragonspine Mountains, the bison-cropped plains of the Grass Sea, the Twilight Marsh, home to lizardfolk clans, the storm-prone freshwater Moonsea and the Quivering Forest, domain of the treants. The Moonsea Lands are dominated by warring city-states governed by petty despots: the port-city of Melvaunt, Zhentil Keep, xenophobic Hillsfar, the frontier town of Phlan and crime-ridden Mulmaster, center of Bane-worship.
The expansionist Warlock Knights from neighboring Vaasa and their Blood Skull orc proxies are a constant menace to the Moonsea.



The Moonsea Lands are a harsh, cold northern frontier made up of the blizzard-prone, ore-rich Dragonspine Mountains, the bison-cropped plains of the Grass Sea, the Twilight Marsh, home to lizardfolk clans, the storm-prone freshwater Moonsea and the Quivering Forest, domain of the treants. The Moonsea Lands are dominated by warring city-states governed by petty despots: the port-city of Melvaunt, Zhentil Keep, xenophobic Hillsfar and crime-ridden Mulmaster, center of Bane-worship.

376.content: The Blood Skulls are a powerful orc tribe based in Bloodskull Keep, Thar. They are highly religious and deeply devoted to the gods of the orc pantheon. The Blood Skulls have an alliance with the Warlock Knights of Vaasa to expand their power over Damara.

377.content: Thar, the Great Gray Land, is a vast, rocky moor with a harsh climate in Moonsea North. Thar is contended by wild tribes of orcs and ogres constantly at war with one another.

378.content: A remorhaz, or ice worm, is a monstrous centipede-like beast native to cold environments. Ice worms generate extreme heat using a secretion known as thrym, useful for magical items.

379.content:
Mulmaster, the City of Danger, is a corrupt, crime-ridden city-state on the windswept shores of the Moonsea, wedged in a declivity between two peaks.
It is a cut-throat place where wealth is held at the pleasure of the Council of Blades and High Blade Jaseen Drakehorn, who rule by the harsh dictates of the Church of Bane.
Any chance to escape poverty (to "move uphill") is seized with the same ruthlessness shown in exploiting the poor: money is sucked uphill to the Imperial District through taxes and bribes, but all that flows back down to the Docks Quarter is shit, if in great quantity: the ancient sewers, infested with monsters and ridden with gangs, are prone to flooding.
Beneath the High Blade's Tower of the Wyvern is said to extend the debauched Palace of Revels. The Brotherhood of Cloaks enforces the city's monopoly on magic and spies on the foreign presence in the Zhent Ghettos and Thayan Embassy.
The Black Lord's Altar is a massive temple to Bane.



Mulmaster, the City of Danger, is a corrupt, crime-ridden city-state on the windswept shores of the Moonsea, wedged in a declivity between two peaks.
It is a cut-throat place where wealth is held at the pleasure of the Council of Blades and High Blade Jaseen Drakehorn, who rule by the harsh dictates of the Church of Bane.

380.content:
Drow are alluring, haughty, hedonistic dark elves from the Underdark with pitch-black skin and stark-white hair. Drow are hated and feared in the surface world for their aggression, violence and scheming; drow consider surfacers weak and hence inferior.



Drow are dark-skinned elves from the Underdark.

381.content:
Kuo-toa are amphibious fishmen with scaly skin, webbed hands and feet and piscine heads native to the Underdark. Prone to fanatical worship of invented gods and mental instability, kuo-toa are suspicious and duplicitous. Kuo-toa live in oppressive feudal theocracies ruled by a priest-king and hate all other races.



Kuo-toa are amphibious men-fish with scaly skin, webbed hands and feet and piscine heads native to the Underdark. Prone to fanatical worship of invented gods and mental instability, kuo-toa are suspicious and duplicitous by nature.

382.content:
The vast network of caverns, grottoes, tunnels, fissures, underground rivers and lakes and magma flows that make up the subterranean world of the Underdark is home to various races such as aboleth, beholders, cloakers, derro, duergar, illithids, kuo-toa, driders, myconids, quaggoth and svirfneblin. The Underdark is divided into levels: the Upperdark, Middledark and Lowerdark. In addition to the drow realm of Menzoberranzan, the Underdark contains the duergar city of Gracklstugh, Blingdenstone, a svirfneblin city-state, the ruins of Chaulssin, and Mantol-Derith, a trading post for Underdark merchants.
The Underdark is a dangerous place for surface races, who are generally not welcome in its depths.



The vast network of interconnected caverns, grottoes, tunnels, fissures, underground rivers and lakes and magma flows that make up the subterranean world of the Underdark is home to various races such as aboleth, beholders, cloakers, derro, duergar, illithids, kuo-toa, driders, myconids, quaggoth and svirfneblin. The Underdark is divided into levels: the Upperdark, Middledark and Lowerdark. In addition to the drow realm of Menzoberranzan, the Underdark contains the duergar city of Gracklstugh, Blingdenstone, a svirfneblin city-state, and the ruins of Chaulssin.

383.content: You prefer to go your own way, without affiliation with any group or organization.

384.content:
The deep gnomes have returned to rebuild the city of Blingdenstone following its sacking by the dark elves.
Between the damage in the war and years of abandonment, there's a lot to do.
The Miners' Guild and their cave badgers excavate barricaded tunnels and caved-in chambers, digging up all sorts of trouble in the process.
The mages of the Stoneheart Enclave, led by Yantha Coaxrock, wards off magical threats, from animated drow statues to rogue elementals.
Trisk Adamantelpiece leads the refounded the Burrow Wardens in their constant battles with the deep gnome wererats of Clan Goldwhisker, led by wily Chipgrin. 
Oozes controlled by the Pudding King, a deep gnome thrall of demon lord Juiblex, are a constant menace to the rebuilding.
Blingdenstone's buildings are hewn from smooth rock, giving them an organic appearance. The Foaming Mug, a tavern catering to foreign visitors, is a good place for adventurers to hear local news and rumors and find work.



Blingdenstone is a recently reclaimed, partially ruined svirfneblin city-state in the Upperdark that still bears the signs of sacking by the drow. Though the war with the dark elves is long over, the efforts to rebuild have just begun, and the deep gnomes have their work cut out for them.

385.content:
Deep gnomes, or svirfneblin, are a suspicious, reclusive underground race native to the Underdark, known for their sullen industriousness, unhealthy obsession with precious gemstones, innate understanding of caves and stoneworking and bitter, bloody enmity towards duergar and drow. Deep gnomes are wiry and lean. Deep gnomes are skillful artisans who create functional structures without ruining the natural beauty of their habitat.



Deep gnomes are a suspicious, reclusive race native to the Underdark, known for their sullen industriousness, obsession with precious gemstones, innate understanding of caves and stoneworking and bitter enmity towards duergar and drow.

386.content: Quaggoths are shaggy, bear-like humanoids with bestial traits, fangs and claws. When not enslaved by illithids or drow, they live in tribes ruled by jalds and psionic thonots, roaming the Underdark in warlike packs and preying on drow and surface races alike.

387.content:
Goldenfields, the Granary of the North, is a vast walled abbey to Chauntea in the fertile Dessarin Valley area of the Savage Frontier. The temple-complex includes a small town of longhouses, home to 5,000 people, the inn Northfurrow's End, Goldengulp Brewery, the lavishly decorated Harvesthome Abbey and its famed farms, orchards and gardens. Goldenfields is tended to by Chauntean clergy and protected by guardsmen, hired adventurers and treants of the Emerald Enclave.
Goldenfields has recently come under assault by a band commanded by hill giant lady Guh, her tribe of hill giants and their allied goblinoid forces.
The goddess Chauntea herself is said to take a personal interest in the affairs of the abbey.



Goldenfields, the Granary of the North, is a vast walled abbey to Chauntea in the fertile Dessarin Valley area of the Savage Frontier. The temple-complex includes a small town of longhouses, home to 5,000 people, the inn Northfurrow's End, Goldengulp Brewery, the lavishly decorated Harvesthome Abbey and its famed farms, orchards and gardens.

388.content:
Dragons, or wyrms, are ancient, powerful magical creatures. The most common types are chromatic (evil) and metallic (good). Dragons live in seclusion or hide their true nature, living amongst other species in polymorphed form.
Dragons are apex predators who eat half their weight in meat each day. Dragons wield powerful draconic magic and project an aura of unbearable fear.

389.content: The worlds in the Realmspace sphere are: Anadia, Coliar, Toril, Abeir, Selûne, Karpri, Chandos, Glyth, Garden, H'Catha.

390.content: Portals are permanent teleportation effects that link places in and outside Toril, including other Realmspace planets and other planes, such as the Ethereal Plane, Astral Plane, Outer Planes, Elemental Planes, the Plane of Shadow and the Elemental Chaos.

391.content:
The Sea of Fallen Stars, or the Inner Sea, is the largest inland sea in Faerûn. It includes the Dragonmere, the Lake of Dragons, in the west; the Dragon and Easting Reaches in the north; the Alamber Sea in the east; and the Vilhon Reach in the south.
The Sea of Fallen Stars is a crucial trade route and is sailed by vessels of Cormyr's Imperial Navy, Sembian corsairs, Impilturan warships and the militia-navy of Turmish.
The Inner Sea is home to many aquatic species, such as dragon turtles, aquatic elves, merfolk, sahuagin, aquatic dwarves, raiks and sidi octupi.
The Pirate Isles are rocky islands in the Sea of Fallen Stars inhabited by pirates.

392.content:
The Kingdom of Damara is a windswept northern region. Earthwood is an enchanted forest of rapidly growing trees cultivated by druids fighting the advance of the Great Glacier. The icy, worg-infested Galena Mountains are home to the rich dwarven mines of Bloodstone Village, the Citadel of Assassins, the Cave of the Whispering Wind and Wyrmsmoke Keep, a cloud giant fortress. The Kingdom is divided into duchies and baronies ruled by Damara's noble houses. The decades-long stand-off between the forces of the Kingdom of Damara and the Warlock Knights in Bloodstone Pass periodically flares into active fighting.



The Kingdom of Damara is a wind-swept northern region. Earthwood is an enchanted forest of rapidly growing trees cultivated by druids fighting the advance of the Great Glacier. The icy, worg-infested Galena Mountains are home to the rich dwarven mines of Bloodstone Village, the Citadel of Assassins, the Cave of the Whispering Wind and Wyrmsmoke Keep, a cloud giant fortress. The Kingdom is divided into duchies and baronies ruled by Damara's noble houses.

393.content:
The Everlasting Rime locks the Ten Towns in perpetual winter. The lakes of Icewind Dale are choked with ice floes, their shores frozen solid. Food and fuel are scarce, imperiling survival throughout Frozenfar, from Bryn Shander, largest of the Ten Towns, to Lonelywood, den of fugitives and cutthroats, Bremen, now too cold for treasure-prospecting, Termalaine, whose ship-builders face ruin, and once-prosperous Targos, where trade is blocked by the snow and ice. Dougan's Hole, Good Mead, Easthaven, Caer-Dineval, Caer-Konig are isolated and increasingly desperate to put an end to the unnatural winter. Human sacrifices and offerings do little to appease Auril's inexplicable wrath, and dark forces are rumored to be taking advantage of the Rime to encroach on the region.



The Ten Towns are a confederation of rugged rival frontier fishing villages along the snowy shores of the lakes of Icewind Dale in Frozenfar: rough-and-tumble trading outpost Bryn Shander, the largest settlement and home to the Ten Towns Council; Lonelywood, refuge of fugitives and cutthroats; Bremen, base for gold-prospectors; Termalaine of the prosperous ship-builders and craftsmen; and its arch-rival, sprawling Targos, bustling with trade and burgeoning with settlers.

394.content:
The Company of Crazed Venturers is a famous adventuring group. Notable members include Khelben Arunsun, Loene, Nain Keenwhistler, Savengriff, Tolgar Anuvien, Dumal Erard, Malchor Harpell and Trunnian Regalis.



The Company of Crazed Venturers is a famous adventuring group based in Waterdeep. Notable members include Khelben Arunsun, Loene, Nain Keenwhistler, Savengriff, Tolgar Anuvien, Dumal Erard, Malchor Harpell and Trunnian Regalis.

395.content: The Arcane Brotherhood is a wizards' guild based in the Host Tower of the Arcane in Luskan. The Brotherhood is a secretive group believed by its detractors to pursue political and economic control of the North and suspected of allowing or even encouraging its members to seek forbidden or dangerous magical knowledge. Though the identity of most members of the Brotherhood is unknown, Archmage Arcane is known to be Cashaan; beneath him are Zelenn the White, Jendrick the Blue, Teyva the Gray and Druette the Raven.

396.content: The Kraken Society is a secret society of thieves, assassins and mages in the Savage Frontier. The Society maintains an information network throughout the North and is led by the reclusive kraken, Slarkrethel. The Society’s headquarters is in the Purple Rocks, and it has a fortress in the ruins of Ascarle.

397.content:
The Savage Frontier is a temperate, rugged rural northern region of remote villages and farmsteads where hearty folk live simply off the land.
The region is home to the famed Goldenfields, walled abbey to Chauntea. 
The largest city in the Frontier is Yartar, a prosperous center of trade and member of the Lord's Alliance.
Grudd Haug is the steading of a tribe of hill giants ruled by Guh.
Spellgard is the ruin of an ancient Netherese Empire castle complex.
The Knights of Samular, an order of paladins in the service of Tyr, have their base at Summit Hall.
The Savage Frontier includes the troll-infested Evermoors, the Dessarin Hills, home to orcs, ogres, giants and manticores, and Far Forest, populated by giant spiders and other creatures created long ago in magical experiments by the Netherese.
Ascarle, the Sunken City, is a lost underwater elven city located off the northern shores of Trisk in the Purple Rocks.



The Savage Frontier is a temperate, rugged rural northern region of remote villages and farmsteads where hearty folk live simply off the land.

398.content: The lost city of Ascarle is located off the coast of Trisk in the Purple Rocks region of the Savage Frontier. Ascarle was swept into the ocean by melting glaciers and destroyed by the drow. It is used by Slarkrethel as headquarters of the Kraken Society.

399.content: Shadowheart is a half-elf cleric of Shaar. She has a mystic wound on the back of her hand. Shadowheart is wry and outspoken in judging others, but also secretive and private in her own affairs. As a cleric of the trickery domain, she favors deceit and illusion.

400.content: Lae'zel is a githyanki soldier from crèche K'liir who serves the god-queen Vlaakith CLVII. Lae'zel is stubborn, self-reliant and a staunch believer in githyanki superiority. Lae'zel is curious about other races, yet cool and aloof, focused on ascending githyanki hierarchy and discovering the truth of her people.

401.content: Wyll Ravengard is a warlock and monster hunter. Wyll was born into a noble family from Baldur's Gate and earned the nickname Blade of Frontiers for hunting monsters under the command of the cambion Mizora. Wyll fights with a magic rapier and has a sending stone as a prosthetic eye.

402.content: Myrkul, Lord of Bones, is a god of the dead, the Reaper who brings souls for the Lord of the Dead to judge.

403.content:
The former confederation of city-states known as Luruar or the Silver Marches has collapsed. The dwarves repelled the orc and drow invasion, but Sundabar was burned in the process. Accusing Silverymoon of stinting aid, the dwarves of Citadel Adbar, Mithral Hall, Citadel Felbarr withdrew, leaving the former members to fend for themselves: Silverymoon, Gem of the North, with its elven architecture and tradition of magic, bustling, mercantile Everlund, where the caravans stop, and the small isolated settlements of Deadsnows, Jalanthar and Quaervarr.
Herald's Holdfast is located in the Moonwood region of the Silver Marches.
The rolling hills and woods of the Moonlands are the territory of various Uthgardt tribes of barbarians.



The Silver Marches are a confederation of cities led by Alustriel Silverhand and made up of the capital, Silverymoon, Gem of the North, with its elven architecture and tradition of magic, the mountain dwarfhold Citadel Adbar, bustling, mercantile Everlund, where the caravans stop, the wealthy dwarven mining settlement Mithral Hall and the militaristic fortress-city of martial Sundabar. The confederation seeks to protect the North against incursions from orc hordes.

404.content:
Located where the Evermoor Way crosses the Subrin near its confluence with the Dessarin, the walled city of Yartar controls trade in the North: wagon trains rumble across its fortified bridge at all hours, and a constant flow of trade barges pull up at its riverfront docks. From her barge-fortress, Waterbaron Nestra Ruthiol takes a hands-off approach to the growing pains of her city's trade-fueled expansion. Ruthiol has aligned Yartar with the Lord's Alliance, but ignores the machinations of the Hand of Yartar, the city's all-female thieves' guild, Zhentarim and Harpers–as long as they don't get in the way of business.
Lionshield Trading Coster is a merchant house with offices in Triboar, Nightstone and Phandalin.
The Fishyard market is a maze of stalls along the waterfront selling fresh fish from the Three Rivers as well as all manner of imported magical goods.
The Happy Hall of Fortuitous Happenstance is a temple of Tymora in a grim stone fortress. The temple often lodges and sponsors bands of adventurers.
The Grand Dame is an opulent riverboat that houses the floating Golden Goose Casino, patronized by Yartar's wealthiest and most powerful residents and visitors.



Yartar is a walled city and trade hub in the Dessarin Valley region of the Savage Frontier. Located at a crossroads near the confluence of two rivers, it bustles with caravans and barges at all hours of the day and night. From her fortified river barge, Waterbaron Nestra Ruthiol takes a hands-off approach to the growing pains of her city's trade-fueled growth. Though she has aligned Yartar with the Lord's Alliance, the Waterbaron ignores the machinations of the all-female thieves' guild the Hand of Yartar, Zhentarim and Harpers activity–as long as they don't get in the way of busines.

405.content:
The towering, impassable Earthspur Mountains rise between Damara, Vaasa, Impiltur and the Vast.
The Earthspurs are home to various human and dwarven mining settlements and bandit camps. In addition to hobgoblins, bugbears, cave trolls, the caverns beneath the Earthspurs may be inhabited by mind flayers.
The retreat of the Great Glacier has freed undead creatures from the ice.
Vast stores of gold are said to be hidden in the Earthspurs. Legends tell of insane prospectors living like animals high in the mountains who attack anyone who ventures too close to their claims.

406.content: Brynwood is a forest in the Vast home to sprites, korreds, satyrs and the Bryndar: evil, magic-using female shapeshifters.

407.content:
The Bryndar are said to be a clan of evil, magic-using female shapeshifters rumored to dwell in Brynwood. The Bryndar are said to take the form of beautiful women to lure adventurers deep into the woods, where they transform into wolves, giant spiders, huge snakes, or owlbears to devour their prey.
Some claim the Bryndar have a hidden magical fortress deep within the Brynwood, where they amass magical resources stolen from wizards throughout the Realms.

408.content:
The Elemental Chaos is an Inner Plane of tempestuous, ever-changing terrain and clashing elements ruled by primordials.
The Elemental Chaos contains the Realms the Abyss, Cresting Spires, Fimbulwinter, the Hidden Realm Muspelheim, Root Hold, Sky Home, Steading, Thraotor, and the Undying Pyre.

409.content: A tressym is a small winged cat with the magical ability to sense invisible creatures and detect poisons. They are intelligent and speak a language of purrs and growls. Tressyms are semi-wild, mischievous little terrors, shy and skittish. They have been known to bond with humanoid races and be kept as familiars and pets.

410.content:
The Church of Bane is a shadowy proscribed sect that spreads His Fear and undermines the political and religious establishment to foment rebellion. Its mages, clerics and agents keep to the shadows, sowing conflict, war and disorder through subterfuge, espionage, infiltration and incitement of mayhem to destabilize realms and then seize control under the guise of bringing order. Favoring ornate black armor, red cloaks and facial tattoos, Banites are calculating, reserved foes who prefer guile over force. The Knights of the Black Gauntlet are an order of Banite crusaders and helmed horrors based in Mintar in the Lake of Steam. The largest temple of Bane is the Black Lord's Cloak in the city of Mourktar in the land of Threskel under Dread Imperceptor Kabbarath Telthau.



The cruel, power-hungry Church of Bane worships and spreads the influence of the tyrannical divinity Bane. Its goals are to sow chaos, undermining the political and religious order to make way for the ascent of the Black Lord.

411.content: Bane is an evil god of oppression, terror, hate and despotism. From his dread plane of Banehold, he manipulates his worshipers and agents to achieve his goal of domination of all Faerûn. Embodying control and ambition, Bane believes the strong have a duty to rule the weak and favors those who conquer new territories in his name.

412.content: Shar, Mistress of the Night and the Lady of Loss, is the goddess of darkness and night and the evil twin sister and rival of Selûne. Shar may appear as Nightsinger, a statuesque woman shrouded in shadows with a mask of feathers who sings hauntingly, compelling listeners to obey, or as the Dark Dancer, lithe, skin black as jet but gleaming with starlight, eyes hypnotic, dance beguiling and sensual, enough to make any mortal fall down and obey her. Shar is mistress of temptation, trickery and manipulation, scheming in the void to warp and pervert all that is good.

413.content: Sharess is the goddess of festhalls, hedonism and sensual fulfillment. Passionate and willful, the Dancing Lady has the independent, hedonistic temperament of a feline and encourages her followers to spread pleasure to all.

414.content:
Baldur's Gate, bastion of tolerance, mecca of bountiful opportunity and bulwark of the Lords' Alliance, is a prosperous city-state on the Sword Coast. The Flaming Fists mercenary company keep the peace under the governance of the Grand Dukes of the Council of Four. The Guild, a clan of thieves run by Nine-fingers Keene, runs the shantytown of the Outer City. The exclusive Upper City is home to the patriar, while in the teeming mercantile Lower City anything can be had for the right price. Beneath it all extends a secretive underground red-light district known as the Undercellar, accessible via various trapdors and passages hidden throughout the city.



Baldur's Gate is a prosperous metropolis on the Sword Coast in the Western Heartlands. Though the Gate is largely neutral, its leaders are stalwart members of the Lords' Alliance. On its teeming streets, the peace is kept by the Watch and the Flaming Fists mercenary company. A bastion of tolerance and mecca of endless opportunity, the city is open to outsiders, be they wealthy merchants, destitute refugees, or even lawless pirates and smugglers.

415.content:
Driders are mentally unstable hybrid drow-spiders: drow from the waist up and spiders from the waist down. Driders are warped beings created as punishment for failing a test of Lolth. Driders lay traps and prepare ambush sites around their lairs. Driders are bloodthirsty, filled with shame at their twisted form and hatred of drow and other races, violent hunters with a death wish.



Driders are hybrid drow-spiders: drow from the waist up and spiders from the waist down. Drow are turned into driders as punishment for failing a test of Lolth. Driders lay traps and prepare ambush sites around their lairs.

416.content: Plasmoids are an amoeba-like amorphous race with bodies of plasma-like ooze. Plasmoids can change their shape and color at will. Resistant to acid and poison, plasmoids can hold their breath for prolonged periods of time and have no internal organs.

417.content: Harengons are free-spirited traveling rabbit-folk native to the Feywild. Harengons have extended rabbit-like feet and ears. Harengons are agile and energetic, with keen senses and powerful jumping ability.

418.content:
Golems are magically animated humanoid constructs. Golems are mindless, emotionless created beings that follow the orders of their creators. Golems can be made from minerals, metals, organic materials and the elements.



Golems are magically animated humanoid constructs. Golems are mindless, emotionless created beings that follow the orders of their creators. Golems be made from minerals, metals, organic materials and the elements.

419.content:
The Shadow Thieves are a vast, prosperous and secretive network of thieves' guilds based in Amn in the city of Crimmor but with operations throughout the Sword Coast. The Shadow Thieves seek to increase their collective influence and wealth. Low-ranking Shadow Thieves might work as beggars, cut-purses, thugs, fences or con artists. Shadow Thieves provide illicit services such as protection rackets, money lending and hired muscle. The Shadow Thieves also run a consortium of smugglers and pirates who kidnap and hold the wealthy for ransom.



The Shadow Thieves is a vast, prosperous and secretive network of thieves' guilds headquartered in Amn in the city of Crimmor but with widespread operations along the Sword Coast. The ultimate goal of the Shadow Thieves is to increase their collective influence and wealth through various criminal activities.

420.content:
Gnolls are savage, predatory hyena-folk with claws and teeth, spotted or striped fur and a crest-like mane. Gnolls live in tightly knit clans and are hostile to outsiders. Gnolls hunt in packs and use scavenged, mismatched armor and weapons. Some gnolls descend from demons and have demonic features.



Gnolls are vicious, savage, predatory hyena-folk with claws and teeth, spotted or striped fur and a crest-like mane. Gnolls live in tightly knit clans and are xenophobic and hostile to outsiders. Gnolls hunt in packs and use scavenged, mismatched armor and weapons.

421.content: The githzerai are a psionic race who long ago escaped enslavement by mind flayers. The githzerai are frugal, monastic ascetics and philosophers who dedicate their life to pursuing knowledge, enlightenment and mastery of martial arts. The githzerai are tall, slender humanoids with pale yellow skin, sunken black eyes and long pointed ears. The githzerai oversee the Obstacle Course level of Undermountain.

422.content: Fire genasi are planetouched humans infused with the power of elemental fire due to their fire genie lineage. Fire genasi have a special affinity for the fire domain and fire elemental magic.

423.content: Earth genasi are planetouched humans infused with the power of elemental earth due to their earth genie lineage. Earth genasi have a special affinity for the earth domain and earth elemental magic.

424.content: Water genasi are planetouched humans infused with the power of elemental water due to their water genie lineage. Water genasi have a special affinity for the water domain and water elemental magic.

425.content: Gelugons, or ice devils, are savage white and blue insectoid fiends with multifaceted eyes, claws, antennae, mandibles and long spiky tails. Gelugons possess ice and flight magic and hate the weak.

426.content:
Elfharrow is a barren, arid region of hot, dry scrubland and desiccated dead jungle dotted with crumbling ruins infested with wild magic and flooded with toxic water. Elfharrow's fierce, xenophobic wild elf tribes defend the withered remains of their homeland with fanatical fervor, preventing looters from plundering the ruins of fallen Lapaliiya.
The largest ruins in the Elfharrow region are those of Sheirtalar, partially flooded and monster-infested. An outcast Aboleth is said to have taken up residence in the ruins of the Palace of the Overking, and cell of the Night Parade is rumored to be active in the ruins.



Elfharrow is a barren, arid region of hot, dry scrubland and desiccated dead jungle dotted with crumbling ruins infested with wild magic and flooded with toxic water. Elfharrow's xenophobic elf tribes defend the withered, blasted remains of their homeland with fanatical fervor, preventing looters from plundering the half-submerged ruins of the cities of fallen Lapaliiya.

427.content:
North Ward is an exclusive enclave of palatial townhouses and luxurious villas. Guard patrols expel the riff-raff from its wide, clean streets and pristine squares. The monster-hunting noble family House Phylund has a palatial compound in the North Ward. The walled estate of House Gost is also located in North Ward.
A murderer has been killing in the North Ward in broad daylight, severing and taking the victims' feet.



North Ward is an exclusive enclave of nobles in palatial townhouses and luxurious villas. Guard patrols expel the riff-raff from its wide, clean streets and pristine squares. The monster-hunting noble family House Phylund has a palatial compound in the North Ward. The walled estate of House Gost is also located in North Ward.

428.content:
Waterdeep is divided into Castle Ward, Dock Ward, Downshadow, Field Ward, Mistshore, Mountainside, North Ward, Trades Ward, the City of the Dead, and Sea Ward.



Waterdeep is divided into Castle Ward, Dock Ward, Downshadow, Field Ward, Mistshore, Mountainside, North Ward, Trades Ward and Sea Ward.

429.content:
The City of the Dead is a decrepit walled graveyard district of Waterdeep littered with shrines, crypts, tombs and mausoleums. The gates are locked at night to keep the ghosts and undead from leaving the necropolis.
Tall, black-cloaked skeletal figures have been spotted stalking the City of the Dead at night.



The City of the Dead is a decrepit walled graveyard district of Waterdeep littered with shrines, crypts, tombs and mausoleums. The gates are locked at night to keep the ghosts and undead from leaving the necropolis.

430.content:
Skullport is a subterranean city hidden within the Sargauth Level of Undermountain. Built in a massive cavern atop an ancient Netherese ruin, Skullport is a rickety vertical warren of stilt-houses, catwalks and scaffolds, home to thieves, murderers and the notorious slaver consortium the Iron Ring. Skullport is contended by gangs such as the Lowfellows, the Mandible and the Xanathar Thieves' Guild. The Crown, its upper tier, is home to wealthy pirate captains. The Venter, its cramped middle tier, is packed with seedy taverns and markets for stolen goods. At the bottom huddles the Dredge, a dank slum. A system of magical locks, operated by the Keepers, links Skullport to the Sword Coast sea caves via the Sargauth River. The Skulls of Skullport are a group of eldritch entities known as called flameskulls, remnants of the original Netherese mages who watch over trade in the city, meting out inscrutable punishment to those who meddle with their domain.



Skullport, the Port of Shadows, is an underground city of thieves, murderers and slave-traders hidden in a massive cavern far below Waterdeep. Its tiered vertical warren of stilt-houses is linked by catwalks and rickety scaffolds, contended by gangs such as the Lowfellows, the Mandible and the Xanathar Thieves' Guild, all under the watchful eyes of the Skulls of Skullport, who brook no interference in their domain.

431.content:
Westgate is a sprawling, seedy port on the Dragon Coast of the Sea of Fallen Stars. It is a den of iniquity and sin, rife in black-market dealings and corruption, where scoundrels and rogues lurk in every alley, where anything goes and everything can be had for the right price. Westgate is ruled by a council of noble merchant families, who elect a leader called the croamarkh. Yet real power is wielded by the heads of the city's noble families: Athagdal, Bleth, Cormaeril, Guldar, Malavhan, Ssemm, Thalvar, Thorsar, Urdo and Vhammos. The Night Masks, a secretive band of thieves, assassins and enforcers, are upsetting the established order. Westgate’s main political enemy is Cormyr. The city's sewers are infested with aquatic monsters, gangs such as the Church of Garagos and Ebon Claws and even a lich.
Westgate is divided into the Old City, Temple District, Market Triangle, Dock District, Shou Quarter, Arena District and the Shore, a coastal slum.



Westgate, where anything goes and everything and everyone has a price, is a sprawling, seedy port metropolis on the Sea of Fallen Stars. Westgate is a cove of pirates, crime syndicates and vampire crime-lords, rife in black-market trade and corruption, with thieves and spies lurking in every alley.

432.content:
Warlocks wield magic flowing from a pact with a being from another dimension known as a patron. The most common types of patrons for warlocks are devils, elder evils of the Far Realm, fey and demons.



Warlocks wield magic flowing from a pact with a being from another dimension.

433.content:
Threskel is a poor, arid land contended by feuding evil dragon overlords. Dracolich Alasklerbanbastos, the Great Bone Wyrm, and his viceroy, the vampiric Jaxanaedegor, vie with the forces of the red dragon Tchazzar. Threskel's windy valleys and stonelands are dominated by Mount Thulbane, a massive active volcano that fills the sky with dark smoke and blankets everything with ash.
Threskel is located on the Sea of Fallen Stars north of rival nations Chessenta and Unther. Mordulkin is a wealthy magocratic metropolis governed by the spellcasters of House Jedea. Mourktar, Threskel's capital and largest city, is a bustling trading port home to Black Lord's Cloak, the largest temple of Bane in all Faerun.

434.content: A cambion is a half-fiend, born of the union of a tanar'ri demon and a mortal woman, usually a tiefling, who typically dies in childbirth. Outsiders to both mortal and demon society, cambions tend to be bitter and twisted, but powerful, ambitious and influential figures.

435.content:
The Iron Ring is a consortium of slavers based in Skullport and Undermountain. The Iron Ring guard unsold slaves, run counter-intelligence against agents of the Lords of Waterdeep and eliminate rival independent slavers. The kingpins of the Iron Ring are the five Iron Lords: Ahmaergo the "Horned Dwarf" (Xanathar Thieves' Guild), Zstulkk Ssarmn, Transtra, Malakuth Tabuirr (Dark Dagger), and Quinan Varnaed (Tower of the Seven Woes).



The Iron Ring is a consortium of slavers based in Skullport and Undermountain. The Iron Ring guard unsold slaves, run counter-intelligence again agents of the Lords of Waterdeep and eliminate rival independent slavers. The kingpins of the Iron Ring are the five Iron Lords: Ahmaergo the "Horned Dwarf" (Xanathar Thieves' Guild), Zstulkk Ssarmn, Transtra, Malakuth Tabuirr (Dark Dagger), and Quinan Varnaed (Tower of the Seven Woes).

436.content: Firbolgs are a strong, wise race of fey-touched giant-kin druidic warriors with bluish-grey skin, wide red noses and pointed floppy ears. They live in isolated egalitarian tribes.

437.content: The Feywild, or Plane of Faerie, is an echo of the Prime Material Plane, to which it is linked by fey crossroads. Suffused with arcane magic and bathed in timeless twilight, the Feywild intensifies and responds to emotions and impulses: sadness wilts, anger withers and joy enlivens. The Feywild is home to eladrin, elves, fey and fomorians, Feywild sparks, firbolgs, eldercaps, Executioner's Hoods and hummingbrellas, moonstone, mirage, faerie dragons, harengon, ogres, giants, and blights. Brokenstone Vale is a kingdom of lycanthropes. Nachtur is ruled by Great Gark, Lord of All the Goblins. The elven stronghold of Evermeet spans the border between Prime and Feywild. The Feydark contains Mag Tureah, cave-kingdom of the fomorians and their servitor cyclops, and Vor Thomil, ruled by the malevolent Queen Connomae. The Domains of Delight are the demiplanes of Archfey such as Titania and the Queen of Air and Darkness.

438.content:
The isle of Evermeet is the last true elven kingdom, a magically constructed island realm protected by illusion, allied sea monsters and Pegasus Cavalry. The heavily forested isle teems with fey and sylvan creatures and is home to the elven capital of Leuthilspar, a majestic city of magically grown glass and alabaster spires of the elven noble houses that sit on the Royal Council. Evermeet spans the border between the Prime Material Plan and Feywild, and the island's settlements are slowly fading into Faerie.



The isle of Evermeet is the last true elven kingdom, a magically constructed island realm protected by illusion, allied sea monsters and Pegasus Cavalry. The heavily forested isle teems with fey and sylvan creatures and is home to the elven capital of Leuthilspar, a majestic city of magically grown glass and alabaster spires of the elven noble houses that sit on the Royal Council. The island's settlements are slowly fading into the Feywild as the elves retreat from the Prime Material Plane.

439.content: Sea elves are curious aquatic elves with blue or green skin, gills on their neck and ribs and webbed hands and feet. Sea elves live in close-knit communal societies based on clan and family located near kelp forests.

440.content: Tritons are a noble, kind but prideful and arrogant humanoid outsider race from the Elemental Plane of Water. Tritons live in feudal underwater kingdoms. Tritons have blue, pearl or green skin, webbed hands and feet and fins on their calves. Tritons are experts with tapals, tridents, javelins, daggers, throwing nets and crossbows. Triton mages use sea shells instead of staves.

441.content: A tapal is an arc-shaped bladed weapon developed by tritons.

442.content: Shifters, or weretouched, are an individualistic, free-spirited race of humans with animalistic senses and instincts who can manifest animal traits such as claws, fangs, fur or tail. Shifters are of mixed humans and lycanthrope descent.

443.content: Tortles are a race of bipedal tortoises from Chult. They have green or blue leathery skin, big hard shells, sharp claws and a beak. Tortles can hide in their shells to protect themselves or to float on water. Tortles are timid, accepting, friendly wanderers living in isolated villages. Tortles believe that their shell is their home, so they never feel homesick and aren't attached to any one place.

444.content:
Chult is a wilderness of legendary riches hidden away in mountainous jungle of predatory plants, blood-sucking insects and parasites and disease-ridden swamps inhabited by pterafolk, bullywugs, yurians, slimes, zygoms, tortles, human tribes, Batiri goblins and hulking dinosaurs. The primordial Ubtao rules over the jungles of Chult, ever vigilant against the threat from under the Peaks of Flame: salamanders, fire creatures, doors to the Fugue Plane, the world of the dead, and Dendar the Night Serpent.



Chult is a wilderness of legendary riches hidden away in mountainous jungle of predatory plants, blood-sucking insects and parasites and disease-ridden swamps inhabited by pterafolk, bullywugs, yurians, slimes, zygoms, human tribes, batiri goblins and hulking dinosaurs. The primordial Ubtao rules over the jungles of Chult, ever vigilant against the threat from under the Peaks of Flame: salamanders, fire creatures, doors to the Fugue Plane, the world of the dead, and Dendar the Night Serpent.

445.content:
The Batiri are fierce, bloodthirsty goblin tribes in Chult feared for their jungle tracking skills. Batiri are experts in jungle lore and nomadic raiders. Batiri worship Chultan divinities with dinosaur avatars, to whom they offer up other races in sacrifice. In combat, some Batiri tribes join up to form battle-stacks up to nine warriors tall.



The Batiri are fierce, bloodthirsty goblin tribes in Chult feared for their jungle tracking skills. Batiri are experts in jungle lore and nomadic raiders. Batiri worship Chultan divinities with dinosaur avatars, to whom they offer up other races in sacrifice. Some Batiri tribes formed battle stacks in combat up to nine warriors tall.

446.content: Malenti are mutant sahuagin who look like sea elves. Shunned by sahuagin society, malenti are raised by nobility as spies or blacksmiths. Some malenti flee the sahuagin and form secluded malenti societies that seek harmony and alliance with other races.

447.content: Sahuagin are a vicious race of muscular, monstrous fishmen with striped or spotted dark green scales, gills, webbing on hands, feet, arms, legs and sides of their head and fins on their back and tail. Sahuagin live in ruthless, militaristic, hierarchical kingdoms in underwater caves. Some sahuagin are born mutants: barons are sahuagin mutants with four arms and dark grey scales that rule over their villages; malenti are sahuagin mutants that look like sea elves and serve as spies or blacksmiths.

448.content:
The Cult of the Dragon is a shadowy web of secret cells of fanatical criminals and madmen who worship and serve dragons. Dragon cultists fill the hoards of their evil dragon masters through blackmail, kidnapping, protection rackets, smuggling, drug trading, prostitution and banditry. Dragon cultists conduct espionage and gather intelligence on the locations of dragons to turn into dracoliches and usher in the rule of undead dragons.
Senior Keepers of the Secret Hoard study the forbidden Tome of the Dragon, conducting magical research to perfect the necromantic Ritual of Ascension, used to create dracoliches.



The Cult of the Dragon is a beast cult that worships undead dragons. The ultimate goal of the Cult of the Dragon is to turn every dragon into a dracolich and usher in the rule of undead dragons over all of Faerûn.

449.content: Half-golems are hybrid living and animated creatures with golem parts magically grafted onto their living bodies. Half-golems are often mindless or insane as a result of the grafting procedure.

450.content: Ceremorphosis is a process whereby a parasitic illithid tadpole slowly replaces its host's brain, causing them to mutate into ceremorphs.

451.content: Ceremorphs are beings mutated by illithid tadpoles. Ceremorphs have illithid powers and traits.

452.content: Illithid tadpoles are small and fish-like with thin tentacles. Tadpoles grow by parasitic ceremorphosis.

453.content: Mind psions are illithids with stronger psionic abilities, including telekinesis, divination and advanced mind control.

454.content: Ulitharids are illithid nobles with stronger powers and longer tentacles.

455.content: Vampiric illithids are feral, mindless beings created by parasitic ceremorphosis of an illithid tadpole infected with vampirism.

456.content: Brainstealer dragons are dragon ceremorphs with purple scales.

457.content: Gnome ceremorphs retain their personality and memories from before transformation.

458.content: Gnome squidlings are failed gnome ceremorphs with small limbs, big tentacles and low intelligence.

459.content: Illithiderro or madminds are uncontrollable ceremorph hybrids of derro and illithids.

460.content: Mindwitnesses are beholder ceremorphs with the abilities of both beholders and illithids.

461.content: Mozgriken are cowardly deep gnome ceremorphs with hunchbacks, three shadowy tentacles, black skin, camouflage ability and no mouth. Illithids use mozgriken as spies.

462.content: Tzakandi are lizardfolk ceremorphs who can spit blinding acid from their tentacles.

463.content: Uchuulons are partial ceremorph chuuls with paralyzing tentacles and skin that exudes corrosive ooze.

464.content: Urophions are ceremorph ropers used as guards and sentries by illithids.

465.content: Yuan-tillithid are ceremorph hybrids of yuan-ti and illithids that have snakes in place of tentacles.

466.content: Brain golems are used by illithids. Brain golems are made from brain tissue and a small piece of an elder brain.

467.content: Cranium rats are telepathic rats that live in swarms. Cranium rats are created by illithids by infusing rats with psionic energy.

468.content: Nyraala golems are large tentacled golems created by illithids by using humanoid flesh, illithid mucus and rare fungus from the Underdark.

469.content: Illitocytes are slug-like creatures with tentacles that hunt in swarms. Illitocytes develop from illithid tadpoles.

470.content: Intellect devourers resemble brains on four clawed legs. They can take over and control the minds of living beings by teleporting into their heads and replacing their brains. Intellect devourers are used by illithids for hunting.

471.content: Probe worms are small worm-like psionic constructs created by mind worms to attack their targets. Mind worms can use probe worms to teleport their prey into their stomach.

472.content: Mind worms are giant pale pink worms created by illithids. Mind worms are immune to acid and magic and can create probe worms to attack their prey.

473.content: Neolethids are giant slimy worms with purple skin and four tentacles in their mouths. Neolethid develop from illithid tadpoles that failed to find a host.

474.content: Nerve swimmers are small leech-like beings that live in swarms, have a shared mind and can control people's nerve impulses. Nerve swimmer are created and used by illithids for torture and interrogation.

475.content: Oortlings are small docile humanoids with big brains created by illithids to use as food source.

476.content: Ustilagors are pack-hunting larval intellect devourers with short legs and two long tentacles that exude corrosive acid. Ustilagors have the psionic power to cause strong emotions in their prey.

477.content: Illithidae are an order of beings from the same alien world as the illithids.

478.content: Cessarids are four-legged, pack-hunting illithidae with slimy grey skin and a beak surrounded by poisonous tentacles.

479.content: Embracs are big, slow ambush predator illithidae with eight tentacles that split in three each, big sharp beaks, short limbs and spotted or striped skin.

480.content: Kigrids are four-legged predatory illithidae with black skin, dull red eyes, sharp claws and spiky poisonous tentacles.

481.content: Saltors are scavenger illithidae with three fingers, white or black skin and ability to use primitive tools. Saltors are used as slaves by illithids.

482.content: The Sword of Kas is a sentient black longsword once wielded by Kas the Bloody-Handed. In life, Kas was Vecna's lieutenant; because Vecna betrayed and killed Kas, the Sword of Kas forever obsessively seeks Vecna's destruction. The Sword of Kas is the only thing that could possibly destroy the Hand of Vecna and Eye of Vecna, provided these two artifacts are grafted to the same being.

483.content: The Eye of Vecna is an artifact that must be grafted into the host's body to be used. The Eye of Vecna replaces the host's left eye, turning golden in color and granting the host clairvoyance, the ability to see through solid objects and the power disintegrate targets by looking at them.

484.content: The Hand of Vecna is the mummified left Hand of Vecna. The Hand of Vecna contains some of his will. To be used, the Hand of Vecna must be grafted on, replacing the host's left hand. The Hand of Vecna grants its host great strength and powerful magic, as well as the ability to kill targets merely by pointing at them.

485.content: Vecna is an intelligent, secretive, tyrannical, power-hungry clairvoyant evil lesser deity immune to mind control feared across the multiverse, worshiped by his vast cult and allied with devils. Vecna used to be a king and later a powerful archlich from Oerth. Vecna appears as a lich missing his left hand and eye, his only physical remains. Vecna's goal is to kill all other gods and consume their power in order to become a greater deity.

486.content: Acerarak is the evil, sadistic, powerful male cambion lich from Oerth feared across the multiverse and worshiped by his cult. Acerarak collects powerful artifacts from the multiverse and hides them in his deadly dungeons full of traps in order to lure adventurers in and gather souls for his philactery from their corpses. Acerarak lives in the Tomb of the Nine Gods in Chult.

487.content: Pseudo-liches are undead mages with necromancy who, unlike liches, lack a philactery.

488.content: Demiliches are powerful liches evolved beyond the need for a body. A demlich may appear as a floating skeletal body part with soul gems that replace some of its bones and act as its phylactery; a demilich may also appear as a floating skull with soul gems that replace its teeth and eyes and act as its phylactery.

489.content: Baneliches are lich clerics of Bane.

490.content: Baelnorns are benevolent undead elves with lich powers.

491.content: Archliches are intelligent, sophisticated and powerful liches.

492.content: Illithiliches are illithid liches disconnected from the hivemind.

493.content: Volothamp Geddarm, Volo for short, is a polymath human wizard, sage, explorer, traveler and writer versed in various subjects, languages and skills and best known for his many guidebooks. Volo is handsome, with fair skin, a well-trimmed mustache and beard, and often wears a worn beret, loose shirt, leather vest and breeches. Volo is prideful, bragging, sarcastic, critical, greedy, verbose and bombastic, but also ambitious, kind and loyal to his friends. Volo can use only weak and moderate spells.

494.content: Astarion Ancunin is a selfish, deceitful, sarcastic but witty and charming vampire spawn high elf rogue from Baldur's Gate who escaped slavery of the torturous vampire lord master Cazador Szarr. Astarion is skilled with bow and immune to sunlight.

495.content: Gale Dekarios is a friendly, gentle, cultured, ambitious wizard from Waterdeep. Gale writes poetry and has a pet tressym named Tara. As a result of a failed magical experiment, Gale has a powerful magical bomb inside of himself called a Netherese destruction orb.

496.content: Karlach Cliffgate is a courageous, fierce but also emotional, energetic and joyous tiefling barbarian from Baldur's Gate skilled with battleaxe and crossbow. Karlach is an escaped champion of the archdevil Zariel. In place of her heart, Karlach has a fiery device called an infernal engine that improves her strength.

497.content: Demogorgon is an intelligent demon lord and lesser deity from the Abyss with a tall, muscular reptilian body, long, forked tail, double tentacles in place of forearms and two mandrill heads. Demogorgon's heads hate each other and have their own personality: charismatic, deceitful Aameul and impulsive, feral Hethrediah. Demogoron can hypnotize, cause insanity and fear, drain life energy, use telekinesis and cause nearby living beings to rot.

498.content: Thornies are small, strong, four-legged, four-eyed beings with thorns on their skin. Thornies are born from mold folk spores and used by mold folk as combat animals.

499.content: Vegepigmies, or mold folk, are a race of small, sexless, noseless tribal humanoid fungi with lidless white eyes, wrinkly skin with color based on their habitat, tendrils on their heads and claws. Mold folk reproduce by infecting and killing living beings with their spores, which grow into mold folk and thornies.

500.content: Myconids, or fungus folk, are a diverse race of pacifist humanoid fungi from the Underdark. Myconids fight with fists or various spores with special effects and control plant and fungi monsters. Myconids come in different shapes and colors, live in the moment, enjoy simple life and form tight-knit communal groups.

501.content: Tren are troglodyte lizardfolk hybrids that live in damp caves.

502.content: Troglodytes are a primitive, sadistic, tribal lizard-like underground race with short legs, long tails, long, muscular arms, small, black eyes that can only see in the dark, a putrid smell and the ability to change color to blend in with their surroundings.

503.content: Derro are a dexterous, intelligent, irrational, insane, paranoid, violent underground dwarf-like race from the Underdark with ragged clothes, blue-grey skin, white, pale tan or yellow hair and white eyes that can only see in the dark.

504.content: Derro savants are sorcerer Derro leaders.

505.content: Chuuls are a primitive, tall, lobster-like race with four two-toed legs, two big lobster claws, a hard yellow-green body and many thin paralyzing tentacles around their mouth. Chuuls live in small groups in underground tunnels. Chuuls hate and eat surface humanoids.

506.content: Oblexes are intelligent ooze monsters created by illithids. Oblexes feed on the memories of living beings. Oblexes create replicas from stolen memories, which they use to prey on their victims.

507.content:
The Nine Hells of Baator is a plane of wickedness and cruelty, organized into a strict caste system with a rigid chain of command.
The levels of Baator are Avernus, Dis, Minauros. Phlegethos, Stygia. Malbolge. Maladomini, Cania and Nessus.

508.content:
Avernus, first layer of the Nine Hells, is the entrance to Baator; Asmodeus forbids the opening of portals to all other levels. Avernus is the staging point for attacks by demon-kind; it was the main battleground of the Blood War.
Avernus is an expanse of barren hills, lava rivers and mountains dotted with rock formations resembling faces twisted in torment. The River of Blood runs through the layer, and everything is covered in a red sheen of gore left behind by the endless fighting.
Avernus is home to Abishai, imps, lemures, nupperibos and spinagons.
The layer after Avernus is Dis.

509.content:
Dis, second layer of the Nine Hells of Baator, contains the infinite city of Dis, an endless smoky sprawl of red-hot iron buildings in a valley ringed by spiked mountains.
The Iron Tower, fortress of Dispater, Lord of Dis, is visible throughout the city, rising above the haze. 
The Garden of Delights offers the illusion of rich food and pleasures of the flesh for an exorbitant price.
Mentiri is the great prison of Dis, which holds those who break the rules of the Hells. Mentiis "reforms" prisoners by tempting them into corruption.
Dis is inhabited by Abishai, imps, lemures, nupperibos, shades and spinagons.
The layer before Dis is Avernus, and the layer after Dis is Minauros.

510.content: Alhoons are illithid liches with dry wrinkly skin and without a hivemind.

511.content:
Osyluths, or bone devils, are sadistic skeletal fiends who serve as police and detectives in the Nine Hells. Osyluths are lesser devils in the infernal caste system.



Osyluths, or bone devils, are sadistic skeletal fiends who serve as police and detectives in the Nine Hells. Osyluths are lesser devils in the infernal caste.

512.content:
Chain devils, or kytons, are sadistic devils that torture the souls of mortals, using their chains both as clothing and whips to lash their victims.



Chain devils, or kytons, are sadistic devils that torture the souls of mortals, using their chains served as clothing and weaponry to lash their victims.

513.content:
Minauros, third layer of the Nine Hells, is an endless bog and decrepit ruin ruled by archdevil Mammon. Minauros is where new souls are processed and minted, a realm of greedy disparity between wealth and poverty, a toxic fen of sickness and despair where everything is slowly sucked into the mud.
Slaves forever mine stone to shore up the foundations of the sinking City of Minauros.
Jangling Hiter is a city in Minauros that hangs suspended by chains from Dis, the second layer, so as not to sink into the swamp. The city is made entirely of chains that sway, buffeted by the winds. It is home to the chain devils, who relentlessly torture all who set foot in the city.
The Labyrinth of Truths is a fortress and record hall in Minauros.
The layer before Minauros is Dis, and the layer after Minauros is Phlegethos.



Minauros, third layer of the Nine Hells, is an endless bog and decrepit ruin ruled by archdevil Mammon. Minauros is where new souls are processed and minted, a realm of greedy disparity between wealth and poverty, a toxic fen of sickness and despair where everything is slowly sucked into the mud.
Slaves forever mine stone to shore up the foundations of the sinking City of Minauros.
Jangling Hiter is a city in Minauros that hangs suspended by chains from Dis, the second layer, so as not to sink into the swamp. The city is made entirely of chains that sway, buffeted by the winds. It is home to the kyton race, who relentlessly torture all who set foot in the city.
The Labyrinth of Truths is a fortress and record hall in Minauros. It is staffed by devil bureaucrats, guarded by barbazu and narzugons and supervised by amnizu. Its records refer to corruption operations, the flaws of mortals, personnel files and infernal cult account books.
The layer before Minauros is Dis, and the layer after Minauros is Phlegethos.

514.content:
Phlegethos, fourth layer of the Nine Hells, is a charred waste of volcanoes, rivers of molten rock, lakes of fire and smoking chasms wracked by tremors. Phlegethos is ruled by Fierna and Belial.
Abriymoch is a city of magma, obsidian, and crystal in the caldera of an extinct volcano.
Phlegethos hosts the Diabolical Court, where all disputes involving devils are resolved. It is also where devils are ritually promoted and demoted.
Jealous Heart, realm of Inanna, is a great field of crimson dust and rivers of blood, animated by passion for war.
The Pit of Flame is a massive flame-spewing lake where devils are punished for their transgressions by repeated immersion in hellfire.
Phlegethos is home to hamatula, cornugons, hell hounds, imps and spinagons.
The layer before Phlegethos is Minauros. The layer after Phlegethos is Stygia.

515.content: Kenku are a selfish, greedy race of wingless, flightless raven-folk rogues. Kenku are acrobatic, dexterous, keen observers with eidetic memory. Kenku can mimic sound and speech and copy texts and objects.

516.content: Thri-kreen are a race of mantis-like humanoid nomads and hunters from Shaar. Thri-kreen are strong, agile, with venomous mandibles and four arms with claw-like fingers. Thri-kreen never sleep and can use psionic powers of mimesis to change the color of their carapace to blend in with their environment.

517.content: Minotaurs are a race of strong, aggressive humanoid bovines with big horns, great sense of direction and navigation and low intelligence. They live in ruthless patriarchal societies hidden deep within underground labyrinths and thick forests.

518.content: A troll's deceptively thin body is covered in thick, rubbery hides colored in mossy green or putrid grey, with long hanging arms ending in massive claws. The skull of a troll is draped with a messy, hair-like growth colored black or steel grey. Female trolls are typically larger, and more powerful, than males.

519.content: Goliaths are a strong and durable tribal race of giant-kin from high mountains who live in strict, competitive societies. They are resistant to cold and have grey or brown stone-like skin.

520.content: Morkoths are sapient, aquatic, carnivorous tentacled octopoidal aberrations with hypnotic and telepathic powers that live in the seas of Faerûn. Morkoths view other races with disdain, suspicion or indifference. Morkoth physiology is an amalgamation of various racial characteristics, with wide variety between individuals.

521.content: Locathahs are toothless amphibious fishmen with piscine heads, green or ochre scales, webbed hands and feet, black or white eyes, and fins on their heads. Locathahs live in protective, close-knit, communal tribes. Former slaves of kuo-toa, locathahs are loyal to their allies and value freedom.

522.content: Rakshasa are evil, selfish, scheming, cultured fiends who use shape-shifting magic to hide their true tiger-headed forms and masquerade as other races. Rakshasa are feared warriors and sorcerers. Rakshasa society is hierarchial, ruled by rajahs, and hidden away from other races by illusion magic. Rakshasa use enchanted weapons and can read minds. When using shapeshifting magic to pose as other races, rakshasa can only be identified by their reversed hands, with palms facing upwards, which they hide to go unnoticed.

523.content: Barghests are intelligent, savage, tyrannical fiendish lupine shapeshifters from Gehenna who consume souls to gain power. Barghests have glowing orange eyes and command goblinoid tribes. Barghests strive to increase their status and improve their strength, size and intelligence with each soul they consume. The most powerful barghests are the size of a small mountain.

524.content: Mordenkainen is a famous multiverse-traveling human wizard from Oerth who lives in Faerûn. Mordenkainen is renowned for inventing many powerful magical spells in common use in Toril. Mordenkainen is bald, with a trimmed goatee, and often wears high-collared grey robes. Mordenkainen is stubborn and does not suffer fools glady.

525.content: Elminster, or El for short, is a famous, ancient, powerful human wizard and sage from Faerûn. El is old, with blue eyes, a long beard and big eyebrows, typically in a plain robe and a wizard hat. El likes good-natured humor and fighting for freedom and hates selfishness. Elminster is intelligent, charming, clever, tolerant, peaceful and helpful, but can be serious, fearsome and arrogant. El can change his personality, turn invisible or magically shapeshift into any person or creature to go unnoticed or take on any role he wishes.

526.content: Halaster Blackcloak is an ancient insane evil wizard. Halaster is powerful, cold, selfish, cultured and meticulous. Halaster created and rules over Undermountain. Halaster is an old man with long beard and hair. Halaster chuckles and mutters constantly, bristles at insolence and insults and satisfies his needs without regard for the chaos he causes or any concern for others. Halaster collects spells and monsters. He controls all the constructs and traps in Undermountain, and can create clones of himself and open portals.

527.content: Coroniir is an elven board game similar to chess.

528.content: Pseudodragons are small dragon-like beings with telepathy, a poisonous tail stinger and chameleon-like mimetic skin.

529.content: Ezzat is an evil elf lich who resides in his library in the Runestone Caverns level of Undermountain. Ezzat has an ebony wand, an amulet that protects him from divination, a companion pseudodragon named Ipses and a sapient staff of frost. Ezzat aims to conquer and take control over the Undermountain. Ezzat is skilled at the board game of coroniir.

530.content: Liches are evil, intelligent undead mages created through necromancy by transferring their life force to a phylactery. The ritual to become a lich includes committing evil acts.

531.content: Vedalken are a semi-amphibious race of intelligent, tall, slender, hairless humanoids from Alara with flat wide noses, blue skin, dark blue or violet eyes and without outer ears. Vedalken study magic like a scientific discipline, strive for innovation and academic perfection, and replace parts of their bodies with a shiny bright living metal called etherium.

532.content: Simic hybrids, or guardians, as they refer to themselves, are super-soldiers created by magically infusing humans, elves and vedalken with traits and abilities of animals. Simic hybrids are created by the Simic Combine, a guild in Ravnica that aims to protect nature.

533.content: Loxodons are a race of strong, tall, patient, friendly, wise, calm, benevolent humanoid elephants from Ravnica with protective tough leathery skin, a long prehensile trunk, elephant feet, four fingers on their hands and a keen sense of smell, intuition and precision. Loxodons are caring and loyal to their friends, but expect them to return the favor and are easily disappointed and enraged by betrayal.

534.content: Kalashtar are a race of serene, monastic, reclusive, kind, caring, stoic telepathic psionic humans from Adar who willingly fused with souls of quori, the evil aberrations from the Region of Dreams. Kalashtar are prone to insanity as they can't handle their conjoined souls of both human and quori. When asleep, Kalashtar see memories of their quori soul instead of dreams as they're disconnected from the plane of dreams. Kalashtar are resistant to psychic attacks and immune to spells related to dreams.

535.content: Leonins are a noble, righteous race of tall, strong and agile lion-folk with thick feline tails, sharp claws and fangs and a menacing roar. Male leonins have thick long manes. Leonins live in nomadic tribes in the plane of Theros.

536.content: Owlin are humanoid owl birdfolk that use broad wing to fly and use sharp talons on their powerful legs to grip things. As birdmen, Owlin resemble owls in face structure, with owl beaks, bird-eyes and plumage. Owlin come in many shapes and sizes, from petite and fluffy to wide-winged and majestic. Owlin are masters of stealth, using their silent flight, night vision and movement to sneak up to their enemy and attack quickly. Owlin speech is punctuated with caws, whistles and other bird sounds.

537.content: Hadozee are a nimble, dexterous race of optimistic, adventurous, joking humanoid apes brown fur, shaggy mane, sparkly black eyes, small sharp teeth, long fangs, prehensile feet and big patagial flaps of loose skin between their arms and legs that allows them to glide. Hadozee are great climbers.

538.content: Giffs are a race of tall, muscular and resilient hippo-folk with chitin plating on their head and snout, great reflexes and movement. Giffs wear uniform or armor and wield ranged weapons or pole-arms. Giffs are traveling mercenaries who organize themselves in hierarchical chain of command, with males and females being equal.

539.content: Autognomes are small gnome-like mechanical constructs programmed and built by rock gnomes. Autognomes are encased in a durable material, can repair themselves and can have different internal structure and tools. Some autognomes serve their makers but others have become self-aware.

540.content: Astral elves live in the Astral Plane. They go into an astral trance instead of eating and sleeping, have a starry gleam in their eyes due to being close to the Seldarine. Astral elves wear ornate armor with face-obscuring helmets and wield weapons infused with radiant energy from stars.

541.content: Kender are jovial, friendly, emotional, curious diminutive humanoids from the planet of Krynn. Kender have pointed ears, short attention spans, a total lack of fear or any instinct to self-preservation. Kender are lock-pickers and rogues who steal out of curiosity and never for malice or enrichment as they don't understand the concept of theft.

542.content: Ed Greenwood is a famous human writer and storyteller from Canada, a country on planet Earth, who collaborated with Elminster on writing numerous short stories, novels and a popular game called "Dungeons and Dragons" set in the Forgotten Realms. Ed is over sixty years old, with long white beard and hair. Ed is joking, passionate about his work and rather eccentric.

543.content: Earth is a planet that exists within a crystal sphere on the same Prime Material plane as Toril. Earth is populated with humans, isolated from most of the multiverse and unaware of existence of other worlds, mostly devoid of magic and magical beings. Humans on Earth use technologies such as cars, smartphones, computers and the Internet. Continents on Earth are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia.

544.content: The Shadovar are the inhabitants of Thultanthar, the City of Shade.

545.content:
Anauroch is a vast, inhospitable desert home to the ruins of the magical Netherese Empire, nomadic Bedine tribes and diminutive, turbaned D'tarig, where merchant caravans battle bandits and shelter at oases, trading tales of the phaerimm, malignant spellcasters living in the Buried Realms beneath the desert, djinn, lamia and asabi. Anauroch is divided into the hot, sandy desert of the Sword, the barren, windswept Plain of Standing Stones and the chilly, arid High Ice desert. The flying Netherese city of Thulanthar is located in Anauroch.

Anauroch is divided into the hot, sandy desert of the Sword, the barren, windswept Plain of Standing Stones and the chilly, arid High Ice desert.

546.content:
The Neverwinter Wood is a dense, ancient forest traversed by the Neverwinter River, which flows down from Mount Hotenow and the Crags range, site of the gates to the dwarfhold of Gauntlgrym. An influx of fey and eladrin from the Feywild to reclaim the ancestral ruins of Sharandar is spurring conflict between the imperialistic humans of New Neverwinter and the local cell of the Eldreth Veluuthra.
Dread Ring, hidden deep within the Neverwinter Wood, is a fortress redoubt of the undead agents of Szass Tam and site of bizarre experiments with necromantic constructs.
The Ring of Swords is a druid circle allied with the Emerald Enclave that guards the forest from greedy adventurers and fights against the hobgoblins, gnolls, and bugbears infesting the ruins of Cragmaw Castle. The crash-landed ruin of Xinlenal, the ancient first flying enclave of Netheril, has been discovered deep in Neverwinter Wood.
